jobs.title: Head of Engineering, Field Verification
jobs.excerpt: Who we areMoniepoint Inc.  is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

Why South Africa

South Africa has one of the strongest engineering communities anywhere in the world, and we are deliberately growing our technology organisation in the country. We already have several team members based here. The work is fully remote, and the mission we are working on is a good deal closer to home than it is for our teams elsewhere.

So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in South Africa.

About the role

Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks — verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors — and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team.

The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out.

We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad — an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA — carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it.

That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one — today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country.

There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business.

As Head of Engineering, Field Verification, your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership.
  • Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development.
  • Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands.
  • Building the operational efficiency layer — trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers.
  • Owning the platform's client-facing surface: the APIs and webhooks that other business units integrate with, and the back office those units rely on.
  • Delivering a native mobile experience for field officers.
  • Ensuring verification data is structured, auditable and fit for compliance scrutiny.
  • Building for multi-country expansion as Moniepoint enters new markets.
  • Partnering closely with Product and with the business units that depend on the platform — onboarding, loans, compliance and fraud.
  • Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and hiring and developing engineers and Engineering Managers.

Who you are

  • You have built things yourself, and grew into leadership from there. We are explicit about this: we are not looking for someone who moved into management early and has led from a distance since. We want an engineer who became a leader.
  • You are capable across disciplines. Backend, web and mobile. This platform spans all three and you will need credibility in each — a specialist in one layer will struggle here.
  • You have built platforms, not just products. Systems used by several distinct groups of users and internal business units, with the flexibility to serve requirements you did not anticipate.
  • You are a problem solver first. We would rather have someone adaptable than someone with the exact domain experience. Having built across different industries — fintech, e-commerce, logistics or otherwise — is a positive signal, not a scattered CV.
  • You have 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on production engineering and strong backend depth. Our backend environment is Java and Spring Boot.
  • You have at least 5 years of engineering leadership, including managing Engineering Managers.
  • You collaborate well with product and business stakeholders, and can translate operational requirements into engineering solutions.
  • Experience working with location and geospatial data is a strong plus, including map integrations.
  • Experience with route, trip or delivery optimisation is a strong plus.
  • Experience building for compliance — where data must be structured to evidence what was done and when — is a strong plus.
  • Experience with identity, KYC or verification platforms is a plus. None of these four are requirements.

Cultural Alignment

As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.

  • Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.
  • Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.
  • Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.
  • Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early.
  • Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders.
  • No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes.
  • Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not.
  • Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.

What Success Looks Like

  • The domain has clear technical ownership and direction for the first time.
  • The team out of keep-the-lights-on mode and delivering against a prioritised roadmap.
  • Measurable improvement in field officer efficiency — more verifications per trip, lower cost per verification.
  • A native mobile experience shipped for field officers.
  • Verification data that stands up to compliance scrutiny across every business unit the platform serves.
  • The platform ready to support a new market.
  • A team grown beyond its current size, with a strong bench of engineers and managers.

Why Join Us

  • A genuinely greenfield mandate on a system that already matters. Every customer Moniepoint onboards passes through this platform.
  • A lean, capable team making outsized impact, and the remit to build the organisation around them.
  • Breadth: backend, web, mobile, location data, compliance and operational optimisation in one domain.
  • Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals.

What To Expect in The Hiring Process

  • A preliminary phone call with the recruiter.
  • 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers.
  • 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes.
  • 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business.
  • 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager).

Qualifications

jobs.excerpt: DescriptionYou ship a benchmark every two to three weeks (example benchmark).
jobs.description:
Description

You ship a benchmark every two to three weeks (example benchmark). Each one measures a frontier risk that nobody has measured yet. Some go public. Some go only to the labs.

Some of the benchmarks and papers are done in collaboration with the leading AI Labs and universities.

You will not write every eval yourself. Each benchmark pairs you with an in-house researcher who owns that harm area, and you get a budget for freelancers you direct. You own the taxonomy, the harness, the quality bar and the release.

The seat sits in the CTO office alongside the research lead who sets our public research agenda. Around 150 researchers here work on harms directly, and you can pull any of them onto a subject.

Key Responsibilities

1. Ship the benchmark cadence

A benchmark every two to three weeks. Size follows the subject. A chat-based taxonomy can carry 100 evals. An agentic or GRPO benchmark is closer to 20, because each one is expensive to read. Sensitivity decides what ships publicly and what goes to the labs alone.

2. Own the quality bar

The test is simple. A frontier lab reruns our set and gets our numbers. The verifiers hold, the rubrics are clear, the distribution is sane, and their subject matter experts read the taxonomy and call it novel.

That means you read the evals yourself. You can screen with a model, and you still open the file, spot the item that does not match the taxonomy, and push the researcher back on it.

3. Run the process

Hold the plan and the calendar. You are the person who keeps other researchers on timeline. You can direct two or three freelancers (SMEs) yourself ad-hoc when needed.

4. Set the roadmap with the forum

Roughly monthly you sit with the CTO and the pod and research leads. Inputs are what our research teams see, what clients are asking for, and what is moving in the news. Output is a revised release plan for the quarter, tied to the accounts we want to open.

5. Stay ahead of the curve

Around 20% of your time goes to the ecosystem. Read the research, keep contacts inside the labs, ask them what is bothering them, and travel to a couple of conferences a year. You should be talking to folks from the labs weekly.

Requirements

Requirements

  • PhD or Masters in computer science, machine learning or a related field, or equivalent depth from industry research.
  • 3+ years building and running safety or security evaluations for language models in production, at an AI lab, a model provider, or a safety and security research organisation.
  • 5+ relevant research publications in the field of AI safety and security including lead author on at least 2 of them
  • Strong engineer. Evaluation harnesses, distributed inference, vLLM, reading a codebase and fixing it.
  • You can build a taxonomy, not only score against one.
  • You can direct a researcher and two freelancers without managing them formally.
  • Strong English, written and spoken. This role runs on internal communication across time zones.
  • Curiosity about the harms themselves. You will be learning a new subject every three weeks.

Ideally:

  • Post-training experience: SFT, DPO, GRPO. Reward design for subjective and safety-relevant targets is a live problem for us.
  • Agentic evaluation experience: tool use, orchestration, permissions, prompt injection.
  • Publications at top conferences.
  • Willingness to present your own work on a client call. Strong communication - both verbal and written, ability to present to large and/or senior audiences
  • Travel to conferences at least 3 times a year

About Alice

Alice is a trust, safety, and security company built for the AI era. We safeguard the communicative technologies people use to create, collaborate, and interact- whether with each other or with machines.

Alice clients are the top 8 AI Labs in the world.

In a world where AI has fundamentally changed the nature of risk, Alice provides end-to-end coverage across the entire AI lifecycle. We support frontier model labs, enterprises, and UGC platforms with a comprehensive suite of solutions: from model hardening evaluations and pre-deployment red-teaming to runtime guardrails and ongoing drift detection.

Alice is widely considered a global leader in online safety and AI security. We have some of the most forward-thinking and passionate minds in the world working to safeguard over 3 billion users across the largest AI and tech platforms.

If you're creative and driven to secure the future of AI, we want to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is looking for a Software Engineer to join our Data Platform team, which owns and develops the core analytical platform across Samsara. This team builds and maintains the infrastructure that powers Samsara’s data lake, distributed compute platform, and the systems that move data from our production data stores into our lakehouse.

As a Software Engineer on Data Platform, you will design, build, and operate reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure for ingesting, processing, cataloging, and accessing petabytes of data. You will work on the foundational systems that enable engineers, data scientists, analysts, and product teams across Samsara to build customer-facing features, train models, develop operational insights, and support the company’s long-term AI and analytics roadmap.

This is a specialized software engineering role focused on data infrastructure. You will work on systems such as Spark and Databricks infrastructure, Delta Lake on S3, data replication from primary data stores such as RDS and DynamoDB, orchestration and metadata services, internal data libraries, and infrastructure tooling across the big data ecosystem.

This role is not an analytics or business data engineering role. If your experience is primarily focused on SQL modeling, BI dashboards, ETL tools, or building business-facing data marts, this role is likely not the right fit. The ideal candidate is a software engineer with deep experience building and operating production data platforms, distributed systems, or large-scale ingestion infrastructure.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
  • You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
  • You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win – together.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate high-scale data ingestion and replication systems from Samsara’s primary production data stores, including RDS, DynamoDB, internal APIs, and event-driven systems, into our data lakehouse.
  • Build and maintain reliable, scalable, and modern data platform infrastructure capable of handling petabytes of data across Samsara’s analytics, AI, product, and operational use cases.
  • Improve the reliability, observability, scalability, security, and developer experience of Samsara’s Spark and Databricks-based data processing platform.
  • Develop internal libraries, APIs, frameworks, and tooling in languages such as Go and Python to help teams across Samsara move, process, discover, and access data safely and efficiently.
  • Work on foundational data lake and lakehouse technologies, including Delta Lake on S3, data catalogs, metadata services, orchestration systems, and platform automation.
  • Collaborate closely with infrastructure, product engineering, data science, analytics, security, and data engineering teams to understand platform needs and deliver durable, scalable solutions.
  • Stay connected to modern data platform technologies and help shape Samsara’s long-term data infrastructure roadmap, including support for AI, privacy, security, global scale, and customer-facing data products.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 4+ years of professional software engineering experience in production environments.
  • 4+ years of experience building or maintaining large-scale production data infrastructure, data platforms, distributed systems, or data lake systems.
  • Strong experience with Apache Spark or similar distributed data processing systems.
  • Experience operating production infrastructure in AWS, including services such as S3, RDS, DynamoDB, SQS, Kinesis, Lambda, or similar.
  • Experience designing, building, and operating reliable systems with strong ownership of scalability, observability, security, and operational excellence.
  • Proficiency in at least one production programming language such as Go, Python, Scala, or Java.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional partners, including software engineers, data scientists, analysts, security teams, and product stakeholders.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, or similar lakehouse technologies such as Iceberg or Hudi.
  • Experience building data replication or ingestion systems from OLTP data stores into a data lake or lakehouse.
  • Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Familiarity with data catalogs, metadata systems, and data discovery tools such as Unity Catalog, Hive Metastore, DataHub, or Amundsen.
  • Experience with orchestration systems such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect.
  • Experience with streaming data, event-driven architectures, or systems that handle late-arriving or mutable data.
  • Familiarity with containerization or orchestration technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, ECS, or Fargate.
  • Experience building internal platforms, libraries, or developer tooling used by other engineering teams.
  • Experience contributing to data infrastructure roadmaps, evaluating new technologies, and driving improvements that create leverage for internal and external customers.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$113,645—$191,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. Role Description:

AI Builders is ShipBob’s new job family — the deliberate next step for Product Management in the AI-native era. The thesis is simple: when AI tools can generate working code from precise specs, the slowest step is no longer the spec — it is the PM→Engineer handoff. AI Builders close that gap by owning discovery, specs, prototypes, and production PRs themselves, accelerated by an AI-native pod.

As a Senior AI Product Builder at ShipBob, you own the full build loop for your product domain: discovery, story/specs, AI-augmented prototypes, and production-ready PRs. This is not the traditional PM role — you are a builder. You use the AI development toolchain (e.g., Claude Code, Driver.ai) to understand ShipBob’s codebase architecture, generate working code against the actual repo, and ship with minimum engineering rework. The minimum technical floor for this role is real: you must read ShipBob’s data model, evaluate AI-generated scaffolding for correctness, and write story/specs precise enough that AI tools can act on them without follow-up questions.

Your domain is Product and Inventory Experience — the system of record for what merchants sell and what they have: the product catalog (SKUs, variants, bundles, kits), inventory records across the network, and the receiving flows that bring stock into it. PIX sits upstream of everything in Merchant Tech — forecasting, placement, allocation, and routing all inherit its data quality. When the catalog is wrong, everything downstream is wrong, which makes PIX one of the highest-leverage product surfaces in the company.

This role is for someone energized by speed, uncomfortable with waste, and who measures success by outcomes shipped — not documents approved. You operate in an AI-native pod alongside talented engineers who are ready to support you and push back on solution when needed. This role reports to a Director, AI Product Builder.

What you'll do:

  • Own the full product loop end-to-end: AI-augmented discovery → story/spec → prototype → production PR → outcome measurement. You are accountable for the outcome, not just the handoff.
  • Own the product catalog and inventory data surface end-to-end: SKUs, variants, bundles, lots, and channel sync. Define the data contracts merchants and partners build against, ship the workflows, and measure data quality and adoption.
  • Run customer discovery yourself; use AI tools to synthesize research across tickets, interviews, behavioral data, and competitive signals.
  • Demonstrate deep functional and technical knowledge of owned products end-to-end. Demo to merchants and partners yourself; understand competitive landscape and key differentiators.
  • Use AI tools to analyze product metrics, identify usage patterns, and surface anomalies. Define success metrics and kill thresholds at spec time — without coaching.
  • Maintain a prioritized roadmap ranked by impact × speed. Use AI tools to synthesize competitive intelligence, market trends, and customer insight into strategic inputs.
  • Evaluate whether a proposed solution fits ShipBob’s architecture without Engineering translation. Understand service boundaries, data structures, and how merchant and partner API usage shapes data contracts.
  • Route changes through prototype-then-PR. Write clear story/specs and review AI-generated code before raising. PR promotion rate improves consistently.
  • Set experiment hypotheses with explicit kill thresholds. Make day-7 rollout/kill decisions on AI-surfaced data.
  • Participate in architecture reviews alongside Engineering as the product judgment seat — the person making the build-vs-buy-vs-defer call on the room’s behalf.
  • Additional duties and responsibilities as necessary.

Your first 90 days:

  • Days 1–30 — Map the domain. Understand the ShipBob operating and commercial mode, examine the PIX codebase, anchor on the purpose and value of the domain, and stakeholder conversations to triangulate the top three active bets. Demo a throwaway prototype back to the pod.
  • Days 30–60 — Ship your first PR. Small and safe is fine. The point is proving the loop, not the size of the change.
  • Days 60–90 — Make a real call. Define and instrument the metric for one real bet, with the kill threshold set at spec time. Make at least one rollout-or-kill call on the data, in front of the team.

What you'll bring to the table:

  • 5+ years of product management, product engineering, or equivalent experience, with demonstrated hands-on AI tool usage in a professional context.
  • Proven ability to write story/specs that AI tools can act on directly — state machines, business rules, data contracts, edge cases — not narrative PRDs.
  • Technical fluency: can read a data model, evaluate an API contract, and identify when AI-generated code deviates from the target architecture.
  • Track record of shipping working prototypes or production code, not just Figma mocks or slide decks.
  • Strong outcome ownership: sets success metrics and kill thresholds at spec time and tracks them after launch.
  • Experience working in supply chain, fulfillment, logistics, transportation, or e-commerce technology.
  • Comfortable operating in a fail-fast culture. Being wrong fast is a feature here — staying slow to look right is the failure mode.
  • Excellent written communication: you write specs, not meeting notes.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with the AI development toolchain (e.g., Claude Code, Driver.ai, Cursor, Replit, V0, Figma AI).
  • Working knowledge of TypeScript, React, or Python — enough to debug AI-generated code and understand what the Engineer is reviewing.
  • Experience with product information management, catalog or inventory systems, multichannel commerce integrations (e.g., Shopify, Amazon), or WMS receiving flows at scale.
  • Prior experience transitioning a product team from traditional SDLC to an AI-native operating model.

jobs.description:
TEHORA est présentement à la recherche d’un(e) responsable technique Solaris senior - niveau 3 afin de contribuer au développement et à l’exploitation de son centre de services Unix/Solaris. La personne retenue prendra en charge les incidents complexes, encadrera les changements à haut risque et participera à la conception des stratégies de migration, de modernisation et de relève pour des environnements critiques.

Sans être exhaustifs, voici les services et livrables que devra fournir la personne retenue :

  • Agir à titre de référence technique de niveau 3 pour les environnements Oracle Solaris et SPARC;
  • Analyser et résoudre les incidents majeurs ou complexes liés au démarrage, à OpenBoot PROM, au boot-device, aux zones, aux LDOM, à ZFS, à UFS, au réseau et au stockage;
  • Définir, réviser et approuver les normes techniques, procédures d’exploitation, plans de changement, plans de retour arrière et critères de validation;
  • Concevoir et encadrer des migrations Solaris 10 vers Solaris 11, UFS vers ZFS, SPARC T-Series ainsi que des migrations de stockage SAN;
  • Évaluer les risques, dépendances applicatives, fenêtres d’intervention et mécanismes de retour arrière avant les changements critiques;
  • Diriger les analyses de causes profondes et produire les recommandations faisant suite aux incidents majeurs;
  • Concevoir ou réviser les plans de continuité, de redondance et de reprise informatique, incluant les RTO, RPO et scénarios de tests;
  • Coordonner les escalades techniques auprès d’Oracle, d’IBM et des autres fournisseurs lorsque requis;
  • Encadrer les administrateurs Solaris de niveau 2, assurer le mentorat et contribuer au transfert de connaissances;
  • Participer à une rotation d’astreinte planifiée et aux interventions critiques hors des heures normales lorsque requis.

Requirements

  • Détenir un BAC ou un DEC en informatique, ou une formation équivalente, combiné à une expérience pertinente importante;
  • Posséder au moins 10 années d’expérience en technologies de l’information, dont au moins 8 années en administration et architecture Solaris;
  • Maîtriser Solaris 10 et Solaris 11, les serveurs SPARC, LDOM, CDOM, Solaris Zones, UFS, ZFS et OpenBoot PROM;
  • Posséder une expérience avancée des environnements SAN et Fibre Channel : HBA, zoning, LUN, multipathing, performance et diagnostic;
  • Connaître IBM SVC, IBM Storwize, V5000 ou V7000 constitue un atout important;
  • Posséder une expérience en migration, haute disponibilité, sauvegarde, restauration et reprise après sinistre;
  • Avoir de bonnes connaissances de Linux, Oracle, VMware, TCP/IP, DNS, NTP, VLAN et outils de surveillance;
  • Une certification Oracle Solaris 11 ou une certification équivalente constitue un atout important;
  • Très bonne maîtrise du français parlé et écrit; anglais technique fonctionnel;
  • Leadership technique, calme en situation critique, jugement, autonomie et excellente capacité de documentation.

Benefits

  • Télétravail et flexibilité selon les mandats;
  • Horaires flexibles et planification structurée des périodes d’astreinte;
  • Projets technologiques stimulants dans des environnements critiques et institutionnels;
  • Environnement collaboratif et multidisciplinaire;
  • Possibilité de contribuer au développement d’une nouvelle pratique spécialisée Unix/Solaris chez TEHORA.

SALAIRE

La rémunération sera déterminée selon l’expérience, le profil et le statut d’engagement retenu.

LIEU DE TRAVAIL

Québec - Télétravail principalement, avec présence ponctuelle chez les clients au Québec. Participation à une rotation d’astreinte et à certaines interventions planifiées le soir ou la fin de semaine.

POURQUOI SE JOINDRE À TEHORA ?

TEHORA est une firme québécoise multidisciplinaire reconnue pour l’excellence de ses services professionnels, de nature technique et de gestion de projets à l’échelle nationale et internationale. Notre mission est d’accompagner nos clients dans la concrétisation de leurs projets par l’excellence de notre savoir-faire et de notre créativité.

Depuis sa création en 2017, notre équipe de professionnels connaît une croissance exponentielle en répondant aux besoins importants en gestion de projets multidisciplinaires, dans le domaine des transports, du génie civil, du TI et plus.

Nos collaborateurs travaillent sur des mandats aussi bien à l’interne que chez des clients d’envergure.

TEHORA se distingue par sa culture d’entreprise, axée sur le bonheur de ses employés et la diversité.

Chez TEHORA, chaque collaborateur est un membre important de l’équipe qui contribue à notre succès collectif. Nos membres ont la flexibilité requise pour avoir un équilibre entre le travail et leur vie privée, tout en menant une carrière enrichissante.

Nous offrons un environnement de travail motivant. La diversité des projets, la grande autonomie et l’interaction directe avec les clients sont appréciées. Une telle proximité est possible en raison de notre structure organisationnelle horizontale, qui se traduit par des relations de confiance et une communication efficace entre notre équipe et les clients.

jobs.excerpt: DLB Associates is a premier engineering and consulting firm specializing in innovative, mission-critical solutions across hyperscale data centers, advanced infrastructure, and high-performance building systems.
jobs.description:
DLB Associates is a premier engineering and consulting firm specializing in innovative, mission-critical solutions across hyperscale data centers, advanced infrastructure, and high-performance building systems. With over four decades of expertise, we partner with some of the world’s most influential companies to design and optimize environments that demand precision, scalability, and resilience.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

Position Title: QA/QC Field Technician III – Connectivity (Telecom / Fiber)

Position Location: Remote - work anywhere in the United States. Must be located near a major airport.

Travel Requirements: Up to 75% domestic travel; relocation may be considered for long-term project needs. Must have a valid driver’s license and ability to rent vehicles.

JOB SUMMARY

The QA/QC Field Technician III – Connectivity ensures that all connectivity infrastructure — including pathways, structured cabling, fiber and copper systems, and network systems — is installed to the project requirements in accordance with the Project Documents, applicable project specifications (including Division 27), the Basis of Design (BOD), and the Quality Control Plan.

This person will collaborate with the client’s connectivity engineer (CE), telecommunications / connectivity contractors (TC), the general contractor (GC), equipment vendors and client staff to validate newly installed telecommunications and fiber / copper network systems, including those in mission critical data center facilities. Monitor daily construction activities and provide timely status reports on project scheduling, Change Order management, contractor conformance to the Quality Control Plan, and Submittal/RFI responses.

The QA/QC Field Technician III will receive general instructions on routine work and detailed instructions on new projects or assignments. May work independently, consistently exercising discretion and independent judgment on individual work, or may work under immediate supervision. May serve as lead on routine projects of limited scope.

This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, as well as departmental objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Assist in Performing On-site Inspection, Validation, and Verification of Connectivity Infrastructure (65%)

  • Monitor daily telecommunications / connectivity contractor (TC) and general contractor (GC) activities, performing continuous independent visual inspection and observation of all connectivity-related work.
  • Conduct inspections throughout project stages, including underground utility / pathway, rough-in, cabling, termination and splicing, and punch list phases.
  • Collaborate with the connectivity engineer (CE), clients, trade contractors, and craftsmen to address coordination issues and installation challenges.
  • Attend and contribute to QA/QC and construction team meetings.
  • Inspect Owner Furnished, Contractor Installed (OFCI) equipment and materials, both offsite and onsite, and support Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) tracking.
  • Evaluate subcontractors’ capabilities in meeting quality requirements. Ensure all trade contractors are following their approved QA/QC plans and do not build upon or conceal non-conforming work.
  • Ensure all connectivity work — pathways, structured cabling, fiber and copper, and network systems — is installed in accordance with project documents, project specifications (including Divisions 01, 07 and 27), applicable codes, standards, and best work practices.
  • Ensure compliance with safety policies and procedures. Complete a daily pre-task plan (PTP) and confirm site adherence to the general contractor’s and client’s HSE requirements during project activities.

Assist in Developing Inspection and Network Audit Verification Plans (15%)

  • Coordinate with the CE and GC/TC to review and align on a finalized list and schedule of all required QAQC inspections across the project lifecycle.
  • Prepare and execute QAQC inspection checklists, providing the final response to all review questions and obtaining the required sign-offs from the CE and GC/TC.
  • Support network audit readiness by verifying contractor pre-audit submittals (quality inspection acceptance, crew and communication plan, communication protocol, and owner-directed procedures), then capture quality data to confirm compliance with established standards or identify deviations and create a plan of action.

Assist in Reviewing Construction Related Design Documents, Drawings and Specifications (15%)

  • Review shop drawings and submittals; support the CE by confirming all project submittals are approved and spot-checking materials and product data on-site against approved submittals.
  • Verify the contractor’s test equipment is correct, certified, calibrated, approved, and in compliance prior to and during testing activities; support witness-testing spot checks as requested.
  • Identify and track key network milestones (e.g., cabling start, circuits delivered, network rack install, CorpNet / Security / FacNet ready and live, Network Substantial Completion and Final Completion) and adherence to the project schedule.
  • Assist the Project QA/QC Manager with a monthly audit reconciling current project specifications (inclusive of change orders) against what the contractor has on hand, and verify fiber and copper test results report the correct pass / loss values per specification. Help manage end-to-end inspection documentation in the client’s quality management platform (e.g., Autodesk Construction Cloud), maintaining control of drawings, specifications, test and inspection reports, vendor data and red-lined as-built drawings.

Position: Sr. Revenue Operations Analyst

Department: Revenue Operations

HighLevel is a cloud-based, all-in-one white-label marketing and sales platform that empowers marketing agencies, entrepreneurs, and businesses to elevate their digital presence and drive growth. HighLevel processes over 15 billion API hits and handles more than 2.5 billion message events every day. With over 2000+ team members across 15+ countries, we operate in a global, remote-first environment. We are building more than software; we are building a global community rooted in creativity, collaboration, and impact. We take pride in cultivating a culture where innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated, and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Every month, our platform powers over 1.5 billion messages, helps generate over 200 million leads, and facilitates over 20 million conversations for the more than 2 million businesses we serve. Behind those numbers are real people growing their companies, connecting with customers, and making their mark - and we get to help make that happen.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

You are a player-coach with genuine analytical depth and a builder's instinct. You do not wait to be asked — you surface what matters before it becomes urgent and bring recommendations, not just observations. You are comfortable walking into a room of experienced GTM leaders and challenging their thinking with data. You see broken workflows as problems to fix, not facts of life, and you have the operational credibility to implement the fix yourself. You thrive on unstructured problems and ambiguity is your baseline, not your blocker.

About the Role

We're looking for a Sr. Revenue Operations Analyst team. In this role, you'll own analytics, reporting, and process for a dedicated segment of the revenue org becoming the go-to person who turns raw performance data into the reporting, programs, and workflows that team runs on day to day. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who's equally comfortable building a dashboard, designing a process from scratch, and troubleshooting a broken workflow, and who wants a direct line of sight into how their work moves the business.

What You'll Do

Analytics & Reporting

  • Own and manage all performance analytics and reporting for your assigned segment, giving leadership a clear, real-time view of how the business is performing

  • Own program attribution — the tracking, operations, and reporting that connect activity to outcomes

Process & Program Development

  • Design, build, and optimize end-to-end processes for your segment, from initial concept to rollout and iteration

Strategic Initiatives & Performance

  • Track performance against goals and KPIs for your segment, flagging gaps early and calling out what's working

  • Build the business case for new initiatives: scope the opportunity, size the impact, and get leadership buy-in
  • Execute initiatives end-to-end, from planning through rollout, adjusting as you go based on what the data shows
  • Report on initiative outcomes against the original goals, and use those learnings to shape what you tackle next

Tools, Systems & Automation

  • Build, own, and maintain the backend workflows and automations that power your segment's day-to-day operations in the HighLevel’s CRM
  • Leverage AI solutions for reporting, dashboards, and analysis

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Act as the analytics and operations partner to your segment's leadership — meeting with them regularly (e.g., weekly) to review progress, surface issues, and align on priorities
  • Support onboarding, training, and change management when new processes or tools roll out
  • Fulfill ad hoc requests from leadership, prioritizing and scoping work independently

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in business/revenue analysis, sales/marketing operations, or a related analytical or operational field
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and SQL; experience with a BI tool (Tableau, Looker, Power BI) strongly preferred
  • Hands-on experience with a CRM (Salesforce preferred) and comfort building within or alongside GTM systems and automation platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

**We support 100% remote, in-office, or hybrid work styles for anyone legally eligible to work in the U.S.

A day in the life:

You'll own a portfolio of 8–12 Core accounts — early-stage and growth-stage brands that are figuring it out in real time. Some launched via crowdfunding. Some are founder-led with no dedicated marketing team. Some are scaling fast, and the infrastructure hasn't caught up. None of them has a budget to waste.

These clients need a different kind of AD. The Power Circuit work is the same, but what you find is usually more fundamental: weak product-market fit signals, an undefined audience, no measurement baseline, and a media mix built on gut instinct. Prioritization matters more here because you can't fix everything at once, and trying to will burn both the client and the team.

You also need to be comfortable being the most experienced person in the room. The client may not know what good looks like yet. Showing them clearly, without condescension, is a meaningful part of the job.

Responsibilities:

  • Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes
  • Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department
  • Run quarterly Power Circuit reviews — diagnose growth constraints across Business, Audience, Product, Messaging, Channels, and Measurement; build a prioritized roadmap that accounts for what the client can actually execute with their current resources
  • Own the senior client relationship, which often means the founder directly; QBRs should feel like a board-ready business update, not a marketing recap
  • Help clients build measurement infrastructure from scratch when it doesn't exist, establish baselines before optimizing against them
  • Coordinate paid, SEO, content, email, and creative work around a focused account strategy; scope management is part of the job
  • Identify expansion opportunities that fit the client's stage, don't oversell services a brand isn't ready for
  • Manage retention and expansion; lead renewals; grow MRR
  • Build multi-threaded relationships with multiple layers of client contacts so no single point of contact departure puts an account at risk
  • Ensure daily use of our proprietary technology (Iris and nova), Pulse (client performance and sentiment tool) cadence at 100%, and Power Circuit (our proprietary diagnostic system) compliance across managed ADs
  • Manage and develop 1–2 direct reports — run regular 1:1s, build development plans, and own their performance reviews
  • Coach analysts and specialists; many will be working with startups for the first time

Role Requirements:

  • 6+ years in marketing, with meaningful experience working with early-stage or scaling consumer brands
  • Has worked with founder-led businesses and understands the dynamic — decisions move fast, emotions run high, strategy and execution blur together
  • Comfortable building from scratch: no brand guidelines, no historical data, no benchmark — and still making good decisions
  • Understands crowdfunding-to-DTC transitions and what changes when a brand moves from Kickstarter momentum to sustainable acquisition
  • Strong prioritization instincts — knows which problems to solve first and which to defer
  • Comfortable with scrappy media mixes and knows how to get signal out of small budgets
  • Track record of retaining and growing accounts, including accounts that went through rough patches

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Expansion to Churn Ratio (ETCR)
  • Net MRR across portfolio
  • Client NPS (8+ avg)
  • Monthly Service Expansion pipeline generation
  • Power Circuit Certification (annual)

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • Team Coaching and Development
  • Marketing Strategy, Development and Execution
  • Client Retention and Client Revenue Growth

  • Base salary + commission opportunities
  • Robust Medical, Dental, Vision insurance plans with up to 100% employer contribution towards employee monthly premium
  • 401(k) plan - 4% employer contribution matching
  • Unlimited Time Off available on day one
  • Up to 4 hours per quarter for paid Volunteer Time Off (VTO) towards philanthropic endeavors
  • Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
  • A one time $100 USD Work From Home (WFH) stipend automatically added to your first paycheck
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • 12 observed United States national holidays + 2 mental health recharge days per year
  • Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
  • Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
  • Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
  • Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

jobs.description:
Contract eLearning Visual Designer

and Absorb LMS Producer

Transforming approved course content into polished, engaging digital learning experiences

Primary Point of Contact: Water's Edge HR Director (Internal Course Manager)

Course Authorization and Prioritization: Water's Edge HR Director (Internal Course Manager)

Classification: Independent Contractor

Schedule: Flexible; hours will vary according to approved project workload and organizational priorities

Location: Remote, with on-site work as needed for collaboration, photography, video, or audio production

Contract Duration: October 2026-May 2027

Estimated Hours: To be determined based on approved course inventory

Position Summary

Central Church / Water's Edge is seeking a creative, technically capable, and highly organized Contract eLearning Visual Designer and Absorb LMS Producer to turn approved course content into clear, visually compelling, and easy-to-navigate learning experiences in the Absorb Learning Management System (LMS).

This is a design and production role, not a course-writing role. Approved Course Content Writers and subject matter experts will supply the course purpose, learning objectives, written content, assessment content, and intended sequence. The contractor will determine how that approved material is best presented visually and technically inside Absorb, while preserving the writer's meaning, voice, and desired learner journey.

The role may include graphic design, page and lesson design, multimedia production, video recording and editing, audio capture and cleanup, and the creation of reusable course templates and visual assets. The contractor will collaborate closely with course writers and the Internal Course Manager, but will not decide whether a course should be developed. Course authorization, sequencing within the organizational training portfolio, and project priority remain with the Water's Edge HR Director.

Role Scope and Decision Rights

The Water's Edge HR Director, serving as Internal Course Manager, authorizes new courses, establishes organizational priority, and identifies the accountable course owner.

Approved Course Content Writers and subject matter experts are responsible for the substance of the course, including learning objectives, written copy, theological or policy accuracy, assessments, and required resources.

The contractor is responsible for the visual treatment, media production, learner-facing presentation, and technical assembly of approved content in Absorb, subject to review and approval.

In this role, the Water's Edge HR Director serves as the primary operational contact, coordinates access and platform standards, and supports final testing and publication workflows.

Key Deliverables

Visual Learning Design and Absorb Production

  • Build and format approved Online Courses in Absorb LMS and, if licensed and selected for a project, Absorb Create.
  • Translate approved Word, Google Docs, Pages, presentation, video, audio, and other source materials into polished digital learning experiences without rewriting or materially changing the content.
  • Create a coherent visual system for each course, including course thumbnails, course posters, title treatments, chapter and lesson graphics, icons, diagrams, infographics, supporting images, downloadable resources, and video poster frames.
  • Organize approved content into the chapters, Lessons, Learning Objects, and course sequence specified by the course writer, using sound visual hierarchy, pacing, and navigation to support the intended learning flow.
  • Use layout, typography, color, imagery, motion, and interaction consistently so learners can easily understand where they are, what matters, and what to do next.
  • Build or import interactive elements, knowledge checks, quizzes, and assessments from questions and answer logic supplied and approved by the course writer.
  • Prepare and upload web-optimized graphics, documents, audio, video, and SCORM-compatible packages when a project calls for them.

Video, Audio, and Multimedia Production

  • Plan the visual and technical production approach for approved video or audio segments in collaboration with the course writer and project owner.
  • Capture high-quality video and audio on site or remotely, including appropriate camera framing, lighting, composition, microphone selection, room setup, and recording quality.
  • Edit video and audio for clarity and engagement, including color correction, audio cleanup and leveling, titles, lower thirds, motion graphics, transitions, music where approved, captions, and final compression for web delivery.
  • Create screen recordings, demonstrations, voiceover-supported sequences, or other multimedia components when they improve the presentation of approved content.
  • Maintain visual and audio consistency across lessons and courses, including reusable intros, outros, graphic packages, and export settings.

Course Flow, Usability, and Quality Assurance

  • Implement the course writer's intended flow and recommend visual, pacing, or navigation improvements when they would make the approved content easier to follow; obtain approval before changing sequence, wording, learning objectives, or assessment meaning.
  • Configure and test learner-facing elements such as lesson order, completion behavior, buttons, links, downloads, embedded media, assessments, and navigation before publication.
  • Test courses in both administrator and learner views, and on appropriate desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes.
  • Apply practical accessibility standards to the visual build, including readable contrast and type size, descriptive alternative text, captions for video, clear headings, keyboard-friendly interactions where supported, and accessible downloadable resources.
  • Identify and resolve visual, functional, media-playback, or responsive-design issues before final review.

Brand, Templates, and Asset Management

  • Ensure each course reflects the appropriate Central Church or Water's Edge brand, visual identity, audience, and ministry context.
  • Develop and maintain reusable course templates, graphic systems, production checklists, and media standards that create consistency while allowing appropriate variation between course types and audiences.
  • Maintain organized source and final files for graphics, video, audio, captions, downloadable resources, and course packages, using agreed naming and version-control practices.
  • Design assets so future updates can be made efficiently by authorized staff or contractors.

Collaboration and Project Management

  • Receive assignments only after the Water's Edge HR Director, serving as Internal Course Manager, has authorized and prioritized the course.
  • Partner with the Internal Course Manager, Approved Course Content Writers, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders to confirm the audience, approved source materials, desired learner experience, deliverables, timeline, review points, and acceptance criteria.
  • Develop a visual concept or prototype when appropriate and secure direction before completing a full course build.
  • Manage multiple approved projects from intake through design, production, review, revision, testing, and publication readiness.
  • Estimate effort, track time and deliverables by project, and provide regular visibility into completed work, work in progress, upcoming decisions, and risks to schedule.
  • Proactively identify missing assets, conflicting instructions, technical limitations, or dependencies and route them to the appropriate course writer or Internal Course Manager rather than making unapproved content decisions.
  • Incorporate feedback accurately and deliver polished work within agreed timelines and review cycles.

This Role Is Not Responsible For

  • Deciding whether a course should be created, when it should be prioritized, or who should be required to complete it.
  • Writing the substantive course content, defining the curriculum, establishing learning objectives, creating theological or policy positions, or serving as the subject matter expert.
  • Changing approved copy, learning objectives, course sequence, or assessment meaning without the course writer's approval.
  • Giving final approval for policy, legal, theological, ministry, or compliance accuracy.
  • Publishing a course as final or assigning it to learners without the authorization required by the Internal Course Manager and the established LMS publication process.
  • Ongoing learner administration, enrollment management, reporting, or LMS governance unless those duties are separately assigned in writing for a specific project.

Qualifications

Required

  • A portfolio demonstrating strong visual design for digital learning, web content, multimedia, presentations, or comparable learner-facing experiences.
  • Proficiency with relevant Adobe Creative Cloud applications, such as Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects, and/or Audition, with the ability to select the right tool for the work.
  • Demonstrated ability to transform supplied content into an attractive, coherent, and intuitive visual experience without assuming authorship of the content itself.
  • Practical video-production capability, including camera operation, lighting, composition, high-quality audio capture, editing, audio cleanup, captioning, and web-ready export.
  • Strong understanding of typography, layout, image selection, visual hierarchy, pacing, brand consistency, and responsive digital design.
  • Strong project and time-management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, stakeholders, and review cycles.
  • Clear communication, reliable follow-through, receptiveness to feedback, and excellent attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently while knowing when a content, priority, or approval decision must be returned to the responsible owner.

Preferred

  • Experience administering or building courses in Absorb LMS and/or Absorb Create.
  • Experience with eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Storyline, Rise, Adobe Captivate, Camtasia, or comparable platforms.
  • Familiarity with chapters, Lessons, Learning Objects, course posters, video poster images, Curricula, assessments, and completion settings in an LMS environment.
  • Working knowledge of SCORM, xAPI, HTML5 course delivery, media optimization, and common browser or device compatibility issues.
  • Knowledge of accessibility practices for digital learning, including captions, alternative text, color contrast, readable layouts, and WCAG-informed design.
  • Experience producing training for staff, volunteers, members, customers, or other mixed internal and external audiences.
  • Experience in a nonprofit, ministry, church, or multi-location organization is helpful but not required.

What Success Looks Like

The successful contractor will establish a recognizable, scalable visual standard for Central Church / Water's Edge learning while giving each approved course the treatment its audience and purpose require. Courses will look polished, feel intuitive, function reliably, and preserve the course writer's intended content and flow. Video and audio will meet an agreed professional standard, learner-facing assets will be accessible and optimized for online use, and course builds will pass review and testing before publication.

Success will also be evident in disciplined collaboration: authorized projects move forward on schedule; content questions are returned to the appropriate owner; project status and hours remain visible; and templates, assets, and source files are organized so courses can be maintained, refreshed, and expanded over time.

At Health Advocate, we’re on a mission to simplify healthcare and empower individuals to make confident, informed choices about their benefits. We don’t just provide answers—we create solutions. What You’ll Do: Your Roadmap to Impact

This isn’t just a call center role—it’s a chance to be an advocate, a problem solver, and a trusted resource. Here’s how you’ll make a difference every day:

  • Guide Members with Clarity & Confidence: Answer incoming calls and emails, providing clear explanations about benefits, costs, and provider options.

Why Health Advocate?

At Health Advocate, we don’t just support our members—we support you. Here’s what you’ll get:

✅ A Culture of Purpose & Impact: You’ll be part of a team that values empathy, innovation, and a shared mission to simplify healthcare for all.

Are you ready to make a difference and become a trusted advocate for those navigating their healthcare benefits? Apply today and take the first step toward joining a team that believes in the power of compassion, knowledge, and service.

This position is primarily sedentary, requiring prolonged sitting while performing administrative tasks. jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD100920

Position Overview

Autodesk Customer Technical Success is looking for an experienced Sr. Customer Advocate, AECO to identify the systemic customer problems that matter most, shape the case for action, and influence decisions that improve customer and product outcomes at scale.

This role will have a strong initial focus on Construction, while operating across a broad and evolving AECO portfolio. The Sr. Customer Advocate, AECO brings together customer advocacy, product intelligence, program leadership, and data-driven decision making to understand what is really happening, determine where Customer Reliability should invest attention, and drive complex issues toward action and measurable outcomes.

A key part of the role is helping establish a more structured listening approach across AECO so we can surface patterns earlier, understand where issues may scale, and avoid relying only on what is escalated to us. You will also help shape how Customer Reliability works across AECO, including how we listen, prioritize, build evidence, engage stakeholders, and measure impact.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Technical Support, Technical Account Management, Product & Support Readiness, Customer Success, and other teams across Autodesk.

Responsibilities

  • Establish and maintain a structured listening approach across key AECO customer, Support, field, Product, sentiment, and data signals to identify, validate, and prioritize systemic customer pain early

  • Build a strong understanding of AECO customer workflows and business challenges, with an initial emphasis on Construction, and quickly develop the product and technical context needed to investigate issues across a broad portfolio

  • Engage customers, customer-facing teams, and internal partners to validate issues, test assumptions, and deepen understanding, using both structured and informal listening mechanisms

  • Synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence into a clear case for action, including the customer problem, scale, impact, strategic relevance, unknowns, and recommended next steps

  • Connect patterns across systemic issues, products, and workflows to build a broader portfolio view of customer pain and help shape priorities

  • Bring structure to complex, cross-functional issues and drive change, aligning stakeholders and ownership, managing dependencies, clarifying decision paths, and keeping work moving toward a clear outcome

  • Influence Product, Engineering, and other senior partners by bringing an evidence-based point of view and connecting customer pain to broader Autodesk and AECO priorities

  • Partner with Product & Support Readiness and other teams to turn decisions and resolved issues into scalable action, including guidance, communication, supportability improvements, or other customer-facing outcomes

  • Follow prioritized issues through to closure and measure impact, including whether resulting actions reduced customer pain and improved productivity, sentiment, or technical readiness

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in customer, technology, product, program, or business environments, with demonstrated program leadership skills and a track record of bringing structure to ambiguity and driving work through to meaningful outcomes

  • Strong analytical judgment and pattern-recognition skills, with the ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence and develop an informed point of view with incomplete or ambiguous data

  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional teams without direct authority and navigate complex organizations where ownership and decision-making are distributed

  • Strong written, verbal, and visual storytelling skills, including the ability to simplify complex customer, technical, and data-driven problems for Product and executive audiences

  • Ability to prioritize a limited number of high-impact issues and maintain focus in an environment with competing customer, Product, and organizational demands

  • Comfort working with data, analytics, and AI-assisted tools to investigate signals, test assumptions, ask deeper questions, and inform decisions

  • Ability to quickly build enough product and technical context to work effectively across a broad and evolving portfolio

  • Brings a collaborative, low-ego leadership style, strong curiosity, and a willingness to work across boundaries to solve complex customer problems

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in or supporting the AECO industry, particularly Construction, with familiarity across customer workflows and technology areas such as project management, collaboration, document and data management, field execution, cost, or construction administration

  • Experience partnering with Product Management and Engineering on product quality, reliability, adoption, customer experience, or roadmap decisions

  • Experience supporting strategic or enterprise customers and understanding the technical and business context behind high-impact customer issues

  • Experience with Voice of Customer, structured listening programs, customer-facing work, systemic issue management, or problem-management practices

  • Familiarity with Autodesk AECO products or comparable professional design, engineering, construction, or collaboration technology

  • Experience developing scalable approaches that reduce recurring customer issues, improve product or supportability outcomes, or drive measurable customer impact

Learn More

About Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Benefits

From health and financial benefits to time away and everyday wellness, we give Autodeskers the best, so they can do their best work. Learn more about our benefits in the U.S. by visiting

Salary transparency

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For U.S.-based roles, we expect a starting base salary between $95,000 and $169,400. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Autodesk, we're building a diverse workplace and an inclusive culture to give more people the chance to imagine, design, and make a better world. Autodesk is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. We also consider for employment all qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable law.


Belonging

The pace is fast, the challenges are real, but the rewards are greater: growth, purpose, and the chance to make a meaningful impact. This is more than a job. It’s a journey on which you rise.

The Engineer will collaborate with the Implementation project team and local Operations & Facilities teams to ensure all actions are completed on-time and in budget.
