jobs.excerpt: Who We AreAt the birth of digital, Claravine noticed a persistent problem with data integrity.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At the birth of digital, Claravine noticed a persistent problem with data integrity. This discovery led to a unique category solution that continues to redefine how top brands and agencies manage the digital experience. We take the drama out of data by standardizing data at the source, giving people, teams, and technology a shared understanding of their data.

What We Do

Claravine is The Data Standards Company. We help brands and agencies deliver on the promise of modern marketing by standardizing taxonomies, naming conventions, and metadata across all digital experiences at the source of data creation. That's why a quarter of the Fortune 100 use our platform, The Data Standards Cloud, to define, apply, and connect standards across their ecosystem for faster decisions, greater agility, and increased ROI.

We Are Hiring

The VP of Product Management leads Claravine's combined Product Management and Product Design organization through the company's growth. Reporting to the Chief Technology & Product Officer (CTPO), this role owns product strategy, and carries commercial accountability for the outcomes that strategy produces: new product and SKU revenue, feature adoption, time-to-value, and Net Promoter Score.

What You'll Do

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own Claravine's product strategy, and translate it into a prioritized roadmap for category creation that balances revenue enablement and innovation
  • Hold the roadmap against Claravine's core capability bets
  • Surface tradeoffs, risks, and dependencies early; recommend a path, then execute decisively once a decision is made
  • Execute the roadmap, ensuring capabilities ship as adopted customer workflows rather than isolated features

Commercial Ownership

  • Own the product's value model — the quantified cost of the customer's current solutions
  • Ensure every roadmap initiative carries a commercial hypothesis, and every new product or SKU launch carries a commercial plan
  • Own new product and SKU launches in service of Claravine's new-ARR growth targets
  • Partner with GTM on pricing and packaging, enablement, and presale motions; be in the field with Sales, not briefing from a distance

Product Discovery & Customer Insight

  • Establish and run the product discovery lifecycle: how customer and market feedback gets collected, analyzed, and turned into roadmap decisions
  • Partner with Customer Success to triage product-related customer challenges and close the loop
  • Maintain working knowledge of buyer activities (planning, activation, measurement) and the surrounding ecosystem (DAMs, DSPs, CDPs, campaign activation platforms)

Adoption, Design & Time-to-Value

  • Own product adoption and time-to-value as primary accountabilities, not just feature delivery
  • Own product design end to end: standards, quality bar, and a measurable UX friction-reduction program
  • Build product and design debt visibility the same way engineering tracks technical debt: known, prioritized, and deliberately traded off
  • Deliver the product capabilities that enhance Claravine's Creative Measurement

Cross-Functional Leadership & Operating Rhythm

  • Operate the Product-to-Market and Customer Success-to-Product decision forums
  • Run the Product Council, where the roadmap gets a commercial review with the customer voice at the table
  • Write and hold the quality bar for product one-pagers, use cases, and specifications that let Engineering start building — be hands-on whenever needed

Team & Organization Building

  • Build and scale a high-performing combined Product Management and Design organization, operating in a startup environment
  • Establish role clarity, career paths, and succession depth across Product and Design
  • Coach product managers and designers through the full product discovery lifecycle

What You Bring to the Table

  • 10+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS and enterprise workflows, including 5+ years leading product managers, with experience leading leaders
  • Domain Experience: an AdOps and MarTech expert who has worked directly with brands and agencies, understands the specific challenges of AdOps, creative, production, and analytics teams, and knows the multi-faceted approaches used to solve them
  • Proficient with buyer activities (planning, activation, measurement) and the platform ecosystem (DAMs, DSPs, DMPs, CDPs, campaign activation)
  • A track record of building complex products that take multiple iterations to become great, in at least two organizations serving a growing enterprise customer base
  • Demonstrable revenue attributable to products or SKUs you owned — not just shipped — including experience carrying a new-product or new-SKU revenue number and being measured on it
  • A track record of pricing and packaging partnership with GTM, and of launches that converted commercially
  • Direct management of designers, or a demonstrated deep working partnership with design leadership, with a track record of raising UX quality in measurable ways (adoption, time-to-value, friction metrics)
  • Experience shipping AI-powered capabilities tied to real, measured customer outcomes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate product direction and build accountability across teams you don't directly own
Salary: $185,000–$245,000

jobs.title: Community Navigator ATTR-CM & Sickle Cell Disease - Great Lakes
jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Pfizer has a longstanding commitment to advancing therapies that improve and extend patients’ lives.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pfizer has a longstanding commitment to advancing therapies that improve and extend patients’ lives. For 175 years, Pfizer has partnered with patients and advocates to develop breakthrough treatments, diverse clinical trials, educational materials, and support programs. The Specialty Care Patient Solutions teamoperatesa patient advocacy support program spanning two critical therapeutic areas – Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) – designed to provide comprehensive care and innovative solutions that support patient journeys in both communities.

Position Summary

The Community Navigator (CN) is a remote, full-time role within the U.S. Patient Engagement Team, reporting to the Patient Engagement Director – ATTR & SCD as part of a national team of eight CNs (sevenfull-timeterritory-based CNs and one floater CN deployed across territories based on business need).

The CN serves as a guide for individuals living with ATTR-CM – representing the majority (approximately 85%) of the role’s focus – and for individuals living with Sickle Cell Disease (approximately 15%), along with their caregivers, helping them understand the treatment landscape and access available resources. This dual-therapeutic-area remit requires the CN to build andmaintaindisease-state fluency, community relationships, and resource knowledge across two distinct patient populations with different patient journeys, advocacy ecosystems, and community needs. This field-based, community-facing position emphasizes patient education, support, and connection to local, regional, and national community partners in both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

The CNis responsible foroverseeing major programs, driving strategic initiatives, and working with cross-functional teams across both therapeutic areas. The CN has advancedexpertiseinthe patientjourney, which may inform organizational direction through key insights that contribute to long-term businessobjectives. The CN adheres to compliance & regulatory standards and fosters innovation to advance patient engagement. The CN is also accountable for measurable outcomes against defined KPIs spanning both therapeutic areas and plays a key role in shaping patient engagement strategies and solutions within the Specialty Care organization.

The CN does notassistwith reimbursement support for Pfizer ATTR-CM or SCD treatments but appropriately triages patients to reimbursement resources as needed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Patient Education and Support:Educate patients and caregivers about ATTR-CM and SCD, treatment options, local and regional support offerings, and health and wellness resources. Provide ongoing education and disease state awareness throughout the patient journey, tailored to the distinct needs of each community.

  • Dual Therapeutic Area Coverage:Allocate time and effort across both therapeutic areas in line with team priorities (approximately 85% ATTR-CM / 15% SCD), maintaining current disease-state knowledge, approved resources, and community relationships in each; flex allocation as directed to meet evolving business and community needs.

  • Patient Navigation:Assistpatients in navigating care by connecting them to relevant resources within their communities and at Pfizer, recognizing the distinct care pathways, sites of care, and support networks for ATTR-CM and SCD patients.

  • Health Equity:Engage thoughtfully with underserved communities, with particular attention to populations disproportionately affected by SCD, ensuringequitableaccess to education, resources, and support.

  • Collaboration:Coordinate with Key Account Directors, management, and cross-functional partners across two brand teams to ensure patient goals and supportobjectivesalign with local market dynamics and patient journeys in each therapeutic area.

  • Project Management:Setobjectives, manage complex projects, and oversee ongoing activities within the Business Unit. Projects may include collaborations and partnerships with Healthcare Systems, HCPs/Educators, and Advocacy partners across both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Expertiseand Knowledge Sharing:Serve as a subject matter expert in both therapeutic areas, adapting and implementing strategic actions. Share knowledge across the organization and contribute to knowledge management initiatives.

  • Innovation and Solutions:Develop solutions to complex problems, champion innovation, and implementnew ideas, processes, or products. Make decisions thatimpactcurrent and future Business Unitobjectives.

Why Patients Need You

Individuals with ATTR-CM and individuals with SCD – along with their caregivers – often face challenges in diagnosis, understanding treatment options, andmaintainingtherapies. Patients in the SCD community may faceadditionalbarriers related to access and long-standing health disparities. Proper education and awareness empower patients to engage in informed discussions with healthcare providers, especially as new therapiesemerge.The CNis thecentral pointof contact in their geography for both communities, focused on disease awareness, education, and connecting patients to resources both within Pfizer and in their local communities.

What You Will Achieve

  • Provide guidance and educational resources to address patient questions and information needs in both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Support patientsinnavigating their care by connecting them to appropriate resources.

  • Share information on emerging treatments and the treatment journey tofacilitateshared decision-making.

  • Coordinate with advocacy and support teams in both therapeutic areas, attending events to present approved educational content.

  • Use motivationalinterviewingtoidentifypatient needs and tailor engagement to each community.

  • Offer both in-person and virtual engagement for opted-in patients,utilizingprint and digital resources.

  • Build trust and provide ongoing support for patients to take informed next steps.

  • Refer patients and caregivers to local health and wellness organizations.

  • Develop solutions to complex problems, influencing long-term goals and outcomes.

How You Will Have Impact

  • Operate within a geographic region to educate and connect ATTR-CM and SCD patients to healthcare resources, balancing effort across both communities in line with team priorities.

  • Strictly adhere to all regulations and policies, collaborating with legal and compliance teams and recognizing the distinct compliance considerations of each therapeutic area.

  • Present the Community Navigator role and Pfizer support resources at local, regional, and national events across both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Partner with internal teams to meet patient needs and provide educational content to support groups in each therapeutic area.

  • Engage with patients and caregivers through various communication channels.

  • Providelocal insights from both communities to inform the development of patient engagement materials and support resources.

  • Organize travel and materials for eventsin a timely manner, ensuring thorough preparation.

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. or B.A. degreerequired.

  • Minimum 7–10 years of pharmaceutical or related industry experience.

  • ATTR-CM and/or Sickle Cell Disease experience

  • Ability to build andmaintaindisease-state and community knowledge across more than one therapeutic area, and to prioritize effectively across concurrent responsibilities.

  • Demonstrated exceptional communication, listening, and presentation skills.

  • Proven ability to work in regulated environments and adhere to compliance guidelines.

  • Track recordof broad collaboration with diverse clients and stakeholders.

  • Experience in responsible business practices and compassionate communication.

  • Experience engaging diverse and underserved patient communities with cultural humility.

  • Familiarity with Pfizer and industry compliance guidelines for working with Medical and Access & Reimbursement colleagues.

  • Ability to deliver concise, meaningful presentations with integrity and empathy.

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational, and business skills.

  • Willingness to travel up to 50%, including weekends and evenings.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills

  • Clinical background preferred (RN, APRN, NP, ARNP, ACSW, LCSW, MPH).

  • Knowledge of ATTR-CM and/or Sickle Cell Disease and patient/public advocacy.

  • Experience with hematology, raredisease, orcardiologypatient communities.

  • Remote/field-based role; preferred to live in specified geography.

  • Bilingualproficiencyin certain areas is preferred.

Other Job Details

Last Day to Apply: September 15, 2026

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $162,900.00 to $271,500.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States.This role is posted in multiple locations. About the Company

Our client is a fast-growing U.S.-based investment management firm building institutional-quality alternative investment solutions for investors, financial advisory firms, and multi-family offices.

The company operates a sophisticated investment platform that includes its own investment funds as well as customized fund-of-funds solutions for financial partners. With assets under management growing rapidly and additional investment products in development, the firm is expanding its operational infrastructure to support its next stage of growth.

The organization combines the innovation and agility of a technology-driven company with the rigor, controls, and sophistication of institutional investment management.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Fund Operations Manager to take hands-on ownership of the operational processes that keep a growing investment fund platform running accurately and efficiently.

This is a specialized fund operations role with responsibility across the monthly NAV cycle, fund accounting, investor transactions, KYC/AML, capital activity, investor reporting, management-company accounting, fund launches, and external provider coordination.

You will work closely with the Head of Operations and serve as a trusted operational partner capable of independently managing critical fund processes from beginning to end.

This is not a traditional back-office role. You will have significant ownership, direct exposure to investors and leadership, and the opportunity to improve and automate fund operations as the platform scales.

What You'll Do

NAV & Fund Accounting

  • Own the monthly NAV process and drive the close through final review and sign-off.

  • Coordinate month-end activities with fund administrators and other external providers.

  • Prepare and review monthly NAVs, identifying and resolving discrepancies before leadership review.

  • Reconcile positions and cash across internal calculations, shadow records, and official administrator records.

  • Manage outstanding manager NAVs and help maintain an efficient and timely close process.

  • Maintain accurate fund performance records, including returns, positions, and expenses.

  • Ensure fund accounting records remain complete, accurate, and audit-ready.

Investor Operations

  • Process investor subscriptions, redemptions, and transfers accurately and on time.

  • Own KYC/AML onboarding processes and maintain an accurate investor register.

  • Coordinate capital calls, distributions, fee calculations, payments, and wire approvals.

  • Serve as a front-line point of contact for investors, handling operational questions with accuracy, professionalism, and discretion.

Investor Reporting

As the global leader in AI-powered customer experience assurance, we help some of the world's most recognized brands deliver seamless, reliable, and engaging interactions across voice, digital, messaging, and AI-powered channels. jobs.title: Community Navigator ATTR-CM & Sickle Cell Disease - Southwest
jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewPfizer has a longstanding commitment to advancing therapies that improve and extend patients’ lives.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pfizer has a longstanding commitment to advancing therapies that improve and extend patients’ lives. For 175 years, Pfizer has partnered with patients and advocates to develop breakthrough treatments, diverse clinical trials, educational materials, and support programs. The Specialty Care Patient Solutions team operates a patient advocacy support program spanning two critical therapeutic areas – Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) – designed to provide comprehensive care and innovative solutions that support patient journeys in both communities.

Position Summary

The Community Navigator (CN) is a remote, full-time role within the U.S. Patient Engagement Team, reporting to the Patient Engagement Director – ATTR & SCD as part of a national team of eight CNs (seven full-timeterritory-based CNs and one floater CN deployed across territories based on business need).

The CN serves as a guide for individuals living with ATTR-CM – representing the majority (approximately 85%) of the role’s focus – and for individuals living with Sickle Cell Disease (approximately 15%), along with their caregivers, helping them understand the treatment landscape and access available resources. This dual-therapeutic-area remit requires the CN to build and maintain disease-state fluency, community relationships, and resource knowledge across two distinct patient populations with different patient journeys, advocacy ecosystems, and community needs. This field-based, community-facing position emphasizes patient education, support, and connection to local, regional, and national community partners in both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

The CN is responsible for overseeing major programs, driving strategic initiatives, and working with cross-functional teams across both therapeutic areas. The CN has advanced expertise in the patient journey, which may inform organizational direction through key insights that contribute to long-term business objectives. The CN adheres to compliance & regulatory standards and fosters innovation to advance patient engagement. The CN is also accountable for measurable outcomes against defined KPIs spanning both therapeutic areas and plays a key role in shaping patient engagement strategies and solutions within the Specialty Care organization.

The CN does not assist with reimbursement support for Pfizer ATTR-CM or SCD treatments but appropriately triages patients to reimbursement resources as needed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Patient Education and Support: Educate patients and caregivers about ATTR-CM and SCD, treatment options, local and regional support offerings, and health and wellness resources. Provide ongoing education and disease state awareness throughout the patient journey, tailored to the distinct needs of each community.

  • Dual Therapeutic Area Coverage: Allocate time and effort across both therapeutic areas in line with team priorities (approximately 85% ATTR-CM / 15% SCD), maintaining current disease-state knowledge, approved resources, and community relationships in each; flex allocation as directed to meet evolving business and community needs.

  • Patient Navigation: Assist patients in navigating care by connecting them to relevant resources within their communities and at Pfizer, recognizing the distinct care pathways, sites of care, and support networks for ATTR-CM and SCD patients.

  • Health Equity: Engage thoughtfully with underserved communities, with particular attention to populations disproportionately affected by SCD, ensuring equitable access to education, resources, and support.

  • Collaboration: Coordinate with Key Account Directors, management, and cross-functional partners across two brand teams to ensure patient goals and support objectives align with local market dynamics and patient journeys in each therapeutic area.

  • Project Management: Set objectives, manage complex projects, and oversee ongoing activities within the Business Unit. Projects may include collaborations and partnerships with Healthcare Systems, HCPs/Educators, and Advocacy partners across both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Expertise and Knowledge Sharing: Serve as a subject matter expert in both therapeutic areas, adapting and implementing strategic actions. Share knowledge across the organization and contribute to knowledge management initiatives.

  • Innovation and Solutions: Develop solutions to complex problems, champion innovation, and implement new ideas, processes, or products. Make decisions that impact current and future Business Unit objectives.

Why Patients Need You

Individuals with ATTR-CM and individuals with SCD – along with their caregivers – often face challenges in diagnosis, understanding treatment options, and maintaining therapies. Patients in the SCD community may face additional barriers related to access and long-standing health disparities. Proper education and awareness empower patients to engage in informed discussions with healthcare providers, especially as new therapies emerge. The CN is the central point of contact in their geography for both communities, focused on disease awareness, education, and connecting patients to resources both within Pfizer and in their local communities.

What You Will Achieve

  • Provide guidance and educational resources to address patient questions and information needs in both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Support patients in navigating their care by connecting them to appropriate resources.

  • Share information on emerging treatments and the treatment journey to facilitate shared decision-making.

  • Coordinate with advocacy and support teams in both therapeutic areas, attending events to present approved educational content.

  • Use motivational interviewing to identify patient needs and tailor engagement to each community.

  • Offer both in-person and virtual engagement for opted-in patients, utilizing print and digital resources.

  • Build trust and provide ongoing support for patients to take informed next steps.

  • Refer patients and caregivers to local health and wellness organizations.

  • Develop solutions to complex problems, influencing long-term goals and outcomes.

How You Will Have Impact

  • Operate within a geographic region to educate and connect ATTR-CM and SCD patients to healthcare resources, balancing effort across both communities in line with team priorities.

  • Strictly adhere to all regulations and policies, collaborating with legal and compliance teams and recognizing the distinct compliance considerations of each therapeutic area.

  • Present the Community Navigator role and Pfizer support resources at local, regional, and national events across both the ATTR-CM and SCD communities.

  • Partner with internal teams to meet patient needs and provide educational content to support groups in each therapeutic area.

  • Engage with patients and caregivers through various communication channels.

  • Provide local insights from both communities to inform the development of patient engagement materials and support resources.

  • Organize travel and materials for events in a timely manner, ensuring thorough preparation.

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. or B.A. degree required.

  • Minimum 7–10 years of pharmaceutical or related industry experience.

  • ATTR-CM and/or Sickle Cell Disease experience

  • Ability to build and maintain disease-state and community knowledge across more than one therapeutic area, and to prioritize effectively across concurrent responsibilities.

  • Demonstrated exceptional communication, listening, and presentation skills.

  • Proven ability to work in regulated environments and adhere to compliance guidelines.

  • Track record of broad collaboration with diverse clients and stakeholders.

  • Experience in responsible business practices and compassionate communication.

  • Experience engaging diverse and underserved patient communities with cultural humility.

  • Familiarity with Pfizer and industry compliance guidelines for working with Medical and Access & Reimbursement colleagues.

  • Ability to deliver concise, meaningful presentations with integrity and empathy.

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational, and business skills.

  • Willingness to travel up to 50%, including weekends and evenings.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills

  • Clinical background preferred (RN, APRN, NP, ARNP, ACSW, LCSW, MPH).

  • Knowledge of ATTR-CM and/or Sickle Cell Disease and patient/public advocacy.

  • Experience with hematology, rare disease, or cardiology patient communities.

  • Remote/field-based role; preferred to live in specified geography.

  • Bilingual proficiency in certain areas is preferred.

Other Job Details

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $162,900.00 to $271,500.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. CACI is seeking a Senior Principal Consultant (HCM Change Management & Training) to lead organizational change management and user adoption efforts for a large-scale federal HCM modernization program. Deploying Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM across multiple federal agencies serving federal civilian employees is not just a technology challenge — it is a people challenge. Every agency has its own culture, its own HR workflows, and its own stakeholders who must understand, accept, and ultimately champion the new system. You will apply structured change management methodologies such as Prosci ADKAR to develop and execute agency-specific change strategies, stakeholder engagement plans, communications campaigns, training programs, and readiness assessments. From initial awareness through full adoption and sustainment, you will be the driving force that ensures this modernization is not just implemented but truly embraced. This role is perfect for change management professionals who want to work at unprecedented federal scale and make a visible impact on how government employees experience HR technology. This position is staffed at the Senior Principal Consultant labor category on the contract. The role carries subject matter authority for its discipline, sets standards and direction, and advises senior stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute comprehensive organizational change management (OCM) strategies for each agency transition wave, applying Prosci ADKAR or equivalent structured methodologies to drive awareness, desire, knowledge, ability, and reinforcement across all stakeholder groups
  • Conduct stakeholder analysis and engagement planning for each agency transition, identifying key influencers, sponsors, change champions, and resistance points across agency HR offices, CIO organizations, employee unions, and end-user communities
  • Design and deliver multi-channel communications campaigns including executive briefings, town halls, newsletters, intranet content, and FAQs that keep agency stakeholders informed and engaged throughout the transition lifecycle
  • Develop role-based training curricula and materials for Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM, covering HR practitioners, managers, employees, and system administrators using a blend of instructor-led, virtual, self-paced e-learning, and job aid delivery methods
  • Conduct organizational readiness assessments at key milestones to gauge agency preparedness for go-live, identifying gaps and recommending targeted interventions to mitigate adoption risks
  • Design and track user adoption metrics including system utilization rates, help desk ticket volumes, training completion rates, and user satisfaction scores to measure change effectiveness and guide sustainment activities
  • Coordinate with functional consultants and subject matter experts to ensure training content accurately reflects Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM configurations, agency-specific workflows, and federal HR policy requirements
  • Support the transition from legacy HR systems by developing side-by-side comparison guides, process change impact assessments, and new-vs-old workflow documentation that helps users bridge from familiar processes to Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM
  • Plan and facilitate change champion networks within each agency, training and supporting designated change agents who serve as peer advocates and first-line support during and after go-live
  • Provide sustainment change management support after agency go-live, including reinforcement communications, refresher training, and lessons-learned capture to continuously improve the transition playbook
  • Participate in SAFe Agile ceremonies as part of the OCM team, aligning change management activities with Program Increment timelines and coordinating with project managers on agency transition schedules
  • Provide thought leadership and strategic direction within the professional discipline, establishing standards and best practices that influence program-wide approaches, and advising senior leadership on matters of significant programmatic importance
  • Lead teams of professional staff, drive innovation in methodologies and approaches, shape cross-functional strategies, and develop talent within the discipline to ensure sustained program capability and knowledge continuity

  • Experience developing and delivering role-based training programs for enterprise software platforms, including instructor-led, virtual, and e-learning formats
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute multi-channel communications strategies for large, diverse stakeholder audiences including executives, HR practitioners, and end users
  • Strong facilitation skills with experience conducting readiness assessments, stakeholder workshops, and change impact analyses
  • Experience supporting federal government IT modernization or transformation programs with complex stakeholder landscapes
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to create compelling content for executive, technical, and end-user audiences

Desired:

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are:Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Role

Serve as the on-duty commander for Alpaca's most critical incidents, directing cross-functional response to restore service quickly, keeping the right people engaged and informed, and making sure every incident leaves behind something the organisation can act on.

You do not fix the outage. You make the response reliable: correct severity, the right engineers in the room, mitigation that does not stall, leaders informed in time, and follow-up work that survives the call.

Things You Get To Do

  • Command incidents end to end. Take command from declaration to mitigation, keeping responders focused on stopping customer and partner impact as fast as possible. Run the bridge, keep observers out of the responders' way, and name a stall out loud when you see one.
  • Classify and hold the line on severity. Set severity at declaration and re-check it as facts arrive. Risk advises on financial and regulatory materiality; the call is yours.
  • Engage the right people, fast. Identify the owning team by service, symptom and blast radius, page them, and expand the responder set the moment the first team is wrong or not enough. When a page goes unanswered, escalate - and escalate the escalation. Bring in the leaders who must make business calls: feature flags, traffic shedding, failover, freeze-or-ship.
  • Hold the bridge, and protect the people fixing it. Keep engineering and technical support uninterrupted - questions from stakeholders, partners and executives come to you. Be the single source of truth to the partner communications team on impact, severity and timing: you decide when a status page update or partner contact is needed, they write and send it, and chasing a late or stale update is yours.
  • Run follow-the-sun handoffs. Deliver warm, high-fidelity handoffs across regions: current impact and severity, mitigation path and next actions, who is in the room, outstanding decisions, and what must not be dropped. The incoming commander confirms ownership before you step away - command never goes dark at a region boundary.
  • Close the loop, on the clock. Maintain the timeline of facts as the incident runs rather than reconstructing it afterwards - in a regulated business that record has to hold up long after the call ends. Once mitigated, make sure a blameless retrospective is scheduled with a named owner and a timebox, and record where the cause sits - that choice sets which follow-up items are mandatory. Every action item needs a real ticket, one named accountable, a priority and a category, delivered inside the agreed service level. If a postmortem produces nothing but low-priority items, treat that as a signal the analysis stopped early and escalate to SRE rather than passing it on.
  • Automate the coordination away. Coordination is the part of this job that should eventually belong to a machine. Every manual prompt you send - the update that is due, the question nobody answered, the partner nobody contacted - is a candidate for automation, and the direction we are heading is AI handling the routine so commanders can spend their attention on judgement. You get us there by working to the decision trees, saying where they are wrong, and being honest about which of your instincts are actually rules.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • 4+ years commanding or co-commanding high-severity incidents in a production engineering, SRE or technical operations environment.
  • You direct technical responders under pressure without being the person writing the fix.
  • You make and defend crisp severity and escalation decisions, and you take charge without waiting to be asked. Command means waking senior people at 03:00, interrupting an executive, and telling an experienced engineer to stop what they are doing - with an audience watching. It is a visible, directive role and it needs to be instinctive.
  • You can read a dashboard and judge for yourself whether impact has actually stopped.
  • You communicate clearly with engineers, executives and partner-facing stakeholders - and you know the difference between briefing the comms function and speaking for the company.
  • You are comfortable holding other teams to account in the moment, across a reporting line that is not yours, without turning it into friction.
  • You thrive in a follow-the-sun model with clean cross-region handoffs.
  • You understand FinTech concepts and the trust stakes of API-driven financial platforms.
  • You use AI tools and agentic automation to reduce manual toil and speed up response.
  • You will work a regional coverage window as part of a global 24x7 Incident Commander roster.

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Formal incident command training - ITIL, Major Incident Management or crisis management.
  • Experience with modern incident management and on-call platforms.
  • You have written severity rubrics, decision trees, escalation matrices, runbooks or incident playbooks.
  • You have commanded in game days, tabletop exercises or incident simulations, not only in production.
  • You have partnered with problem management or reliability programme functions to roadmap incident follow-ups.
  • Online securities trading or capital markets experience, or another regulated, market-hours-sensitive domain.

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

Bei uns gestaltest du Wachstum nicht mit – du verantwortest es.
Du arbeitest eng mit dem Gründer (Bastian) zusammen, entwickelst skalierbare Content-Strategien und baust Social Media als messbaren Wachstumskanal aus.

Wenn du Performance liebst, Daten ernst nimmst und Social Media als strategisches Spielfeld verstehst – dann sollten wir sprechen.

Aufgaben

Qualifikation

  • Copywriting: Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Sprache und Erfahrung im Verfassen von überzeugenden, zielgruppengerechten Texten für unterschiedliche Formate und Plattformen.
  • Mindset:
    Growth ist für dich kein Buzzword. Du denkst in KPIs, Conversion, Retention und Skalierung.
  • Plattform-Verständnis:
    Du verstehst die Algorithmen von Instagram, YouTube und TikTok nicht nur oberflächlich, sondern strategisch.

    Du arbeitest sicher mit Analytics-Tools wie Instagram Insights, YouTube Analytics etc. und leitest daraus konkrete Handlungen ab.
  • Strategie + Kreativität:
    Du kannst virale Ideen entwickeln – aber immer mit einem klaren strategischen Ziel.
  • Arbeitsweise:
    Eigenständig, strukturiert, verantwortungsvoll. Kein Micromanagement nötig.

Benefits

  • Volle Verantwortung für spannende Kanäle mit Wachstumspotenzial
  • Ein Team aus Top-Performern und Gründer:innen, das gemeinsam auf Wachstum setzt.

Hat dich das überzeugt ?

Dann bewirb dich jetzt und starte bald gemeinsam mit uns durch! Lade einfach deinen Lebenslauf hoch – ein Anschreiben oder Zeugnisse sind überflüssig. Wir halten es lieber unkompliziert.

Competence-Call: Als nächstes lernst du deinen Teamlead kennen. In einem 60–75-minütigen Gespräch sprechen wir über deine fachlichen und persönlichen Stärken – und finden gemeinsam heraus, ob es ein Match zwischen uns gibt. Nach dem Call bekommst du schnellstmöglich unser Feedback.

Founder Call: Zum Abschluss möchte dich unser Co-Founder Sam persönlich kennenlernen (ca. 30 min.). Keine Sorge – du bekommst innerhalb von 2 Tagen Feedback. Wenn alles passt, starten wir gemeinsam durch!

  • Expert-level proficiency of Python

  • Strong experience with Azure data services (Azure SQL, Data Factory, Synapse, Blob Storage, etc.)

  • Knowledge of Power BI development skills including DAX, data modeling, and performance optimization
  • Solid understanding of database design principles, normalization, and data modeling
  • Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD practices
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment
  • Microsoft certification (Azure Data Engineer Associate, Azure Database Administrator, Power BI Data Analyst)
  • Knowledge of Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Bicep, ARM templates)
  • Knowledge of additional Azure services (Container Apps, Functions, Logic Apps)

jobs.description:
About Us:

The Competency & Credentialing Institute (CCI) has been the leader in perioperative certification for more than 45 years, certifying over 40,000 nurses internationally. An industry leader in nursing competency assessment, CCI is the credentialing body for the Certified Perioperative Nurse (CNOR), Certified Surgical Services Manager (CSSM), Certified Perioperative CNS (CNS-CP), Certified Ambulatory Surgery Nurse (CNAMB), Certified Foundational Perioperative Nurse (CFPN), and Nursing Professional Development Advanced – Board Certified (NPDA-BC) credentials.

Job Summary:

The Technology Systems Analyst plays a critical role in supporting and advancing CCI’s technology infrastructure and vendor ecosystem. They serve as CCI’s central hub for system integrations, vendor coordination, and technology risk oversight. This role bridges business needs, internal systems, external vendors, and internal employees ensuring platforms work together effectively without requiring in-house development. 
The analyst proactively monitors system performance, integration health, and security posture, identifying risks and driving mitigation strategies across CCI’s technology ecosystem. The analyst will also assist with internal audits and quality assurance processes, while proactively researching and recommending emerging technologies that align with CCI’s strategic goals. The role requires strong systems thinking, with the ability to anticipate downstream impacts of changes, identify vulnerabilities, and drive mitigation strategies.

Roles & Responsibilities:

Systems Administration, Integration & Support

  • Administer and maintain core technology systems and platforms, ensuring reliability, stability, and performance
  • Map, document, and maintain visibility into system integrations, data flows, and dependencies across CCI platforms (e.g., CMS, LMS, CRM, finance systems)
  • Evaluate the downstream impact of system updates, configuration changes, and new features across integrated platforms
  • Validate and test integration outputs (data accuracy, timing, failure points) in collaboration with vendors
  • Troubleshoot cross-system issues and drive root-cause analysis across multiple platforms
  • Provide application support and guidance to staff, promoting effective and optimized use of systems
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand business needs and support system enhancements
  • Identify and reduce friction in system access, workflows, and support processes
  • Curate and maintain system documentation, including knowledgebase resources and process guides

Vendor Management, Security & Technology Governance

  • Serve as the primary liaison between internal stakeholders and vendors on integration design, changes, and issue resolution
  • Act as the technical point of accountability for vendor-delivered functionality, integrations, and system performance
  • Translate business requirements into clear technical expectations for vendors
  • Review vendor proposals, deliverables, and change requests for feasibility, impact, and alignment with system architecture
  • Identify risks related to cost, scope, timelines, technical approach, and security; escalate concerns as needed
  • Provide technical insight to support contract negotiations, renewals, and scope validation
  • Proactively monitor system security posture, vulnerabilities, and risks across platforms
  • Review and interpret third-party security reports (e.g., SOC 2, penetration tests, vulnerability scans) and translate findings into actionable insights
  • Assess vendor security practices and identify gaps relative to organizational expectations and compliance requirements
  • Collaborate with vendors to track and remediate vulnerabilities and ensure resolution
  • Stay informed on emerging security risks and recommend preventative controls
  • Support the development and enforcement of internal security standards, procedures, and incident response practices

Technology Strategy, Projects & Continuous Improvement

  • Support small to mid-sized IT projects and system change initiatives
  • Assist with internal audits, quality assurance reviews, and documentation of technology processes
  • Contribute to governance of emerging technologies, including AI tools and automation platforms
  • Research and evaluate new technologies to improve efficiency, integration, or service delivery
  • Recommend solutions that reduce manual work, improve data integrity, or enhance system connectivity
  • Drive workflow and process optimization with AI and other technologies

Required Skills & Abilities:

  • Experience working in multi-system environments with integrations across platforms (e.g., CMS, LMS, CRM, finance systems, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Egnyte Secure Cloud Storage, CRM/CMS platforms, financial systems (e.g., Sage Intacct), learning platforms (LMS), AI productivity tools (e.g., Copilot), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira ITSM, Confluence Knowledgebase)
  • Strong understanding of system interdependencies and the downstream impact of changes
  • Values aligned with non-profit work and small businesses
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity principles and third-party risk management
  • Experience reviewing or interpreting vendor security and compliance documentation is preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a technical translator between business stakeholders and external vendors
  • Experience leading or contributing to IT projects and change initiatives
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating across teams

Education & Experience:

  • Minimum of three (3+) years’ working experience in systems administration, IT operations, or technical vendor management
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field preferred. Relevant technical certifications, formal training, or comparable professional experience may be substituted.

Benefits & Perks:

CCI offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees' health and well-being. Eligible employees may receive:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life, and AD&D insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company matching and safe harbor contributions
  • Paid time off and paid holidays in accordance with applicable state laws
  • Professional development opportunities and employer-supported continuing education

Compensation:

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $70,000–$113,000, depending on qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

For applicants who will perform this position in Colorado, the anticipated annual salary range is $83,700 – $113,000.

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, internal equity, and market considerations.

Applications will be accepted through September 15, 2026. The application deadline may be extended based on business needs.

This position is open to applicants in Colorado, Texas, North Carolina, and Minnesota.

Competency & Credentialing Institute is dedicated to the principles of Equal Employment Opportunity. The Company is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race (including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religious creed, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity and expression, national origin, citizenship status, ancestry, marital status, medical condition (as defined by applicable law, e.g., cancer or genetic characteristics), physical and mental disability, pregnancy (including childbirth and related medical conditions), military service, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected status in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

About VyOS Networks

VyOS Networks is the company behind VyOS, the enterprise-grade open source networking platform for bare metal, cloud, and edge. VyOS powers mission-critical connectivity for enterprises, service providers, and governments worldwide, and is available across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and other cloud platforms. Our mission is to return full control and ownership of network infrastructure to our users.

Job description

We have a capable support team today. It handles escalations, meets SLAs, and delivers quality answers. What it is not built for is serving thousands of subscription customers. We are hiring someone who has already made that transition at another technology company and knows how to do it here.

This is not a role for someone who wants to learn how to scale support. It is a role for someone who has done it, hit the predictable walls (tooling that collapses under volume, tier-1 burnout, knowledge trapped in senior engineers' heads, SLA models that don't survive 10x growth, hiring pipelines that can't keep pace), and knows which problems to solve before they appear.

You will own the support function end to end: strategy, structure, tooling, hiring, metrics, and economics. You will inherit a working team and transform it into a scalable operation.

What you will do

  • Design and execute the plan to scale support from hundreds to thousands of customers without degrading response quality or blowing up cost per customer
  • Build a tiered support model with clear ownership boundaries, escalation paths, and handoff criteria between tiers
  • Drive ticket deflection: knowledge base, documentation feedback loops into engineering, self-service, and community channels
  • Deploy and own support tooling, including automation and AI-assisted resolution for tier-1 volume. Our support stack runs on Jira Service Management, and you will own its configuration, workflows, SLAs, and portal
  • Define the metrics that matter (time to resolution, first-contact resolution, deflection rate, CSAT, cost per ticket) and run the function on them
  • Build the hiring plan and career paths needed for follow-the-sun coverage across regions
  • Turn support data into product signal: recurring issues feed engineering priorities, not just ticket queues
  • Own SLA design and delivery for customers with different contractual commitments
  • Turn support interactions into market and customer insight: use AI-assisted analysis of tickets, escalations, and product usage patterns to surface trends in customer needs, competitive pressure, and expansion opportunity, and share these systematically with product, marketing, and sales
  • Manage an AI-assisted lead generation motion out of support: identify and qualify signals in support conversations that indicate a need for professional services (implementation help, custom integrations, training, advanced configuration), and route them into a repeatable pipeline that grows the professional services revenue stream
  • Work directly with sales, customer success, and engineering leadership on renewals at risk, escalated accounts, and support-driven expansion

Mandatory requirements

We will not consider candidates without these.

  • You have scaled a technical support organization at a technology company from hundreds to thousands of customers, and you can walk us through exactly what you changed, what broke, and what you would do differently
  • You have managed managers, not just individual contributors, and built team structure across time zones
  • You have owned support economics: headcount planning, cost per ticket, and the deflection and automation work that keeps costs sub-linear to customer growth
  • You have implemented or replaced support tooling at scale (ticketing, knowledge management, customer portals) and lived with the consequences. Working knowledge of Jira Service Management (queues, SLAs, automation rules, customer portal) or the demonstrated ability to master it fast
  • Deep familiarity with B2B technical support for infrastructure or networking products, where customers are engineers and wrong answers cause outages

Strong pluses

  • Experience supporting open-source software commercially, where the line between community and paying customer matters
  • Networking domain knowledge (routing, VPN, firewalling) or experience supporting a network OS, NOS vendor, or adjacent infrastructure product
  • Hands-on experience deploying AI agents or automation for tier-1 ticket resolution
  • Advanced Jira Service Management administration: workflow design, automation, asset/CMDB integration, and reporting across Jira and Confluence
  • Experience supporting OEM and embedded customers with redistribution agreements

What we are not looking for

  • Someone whose scaling experience is theoretical, secondhand, or limited to consumer support
  • A pure people manager who delegates all technical and tooling decisions
  • Someone who needs the playbook handed to them. You bring the playbook.

How we evaluate

The interview process centers on your track record. Expect to present a specific scaling case from your career: the starting state, the decisions you made, the mistakes, the metrics before and after. References will be checked against it.

Our Mission

Powering a connected world, engineering for the future.

We believe that the future of networking lies in open collaboration, continuous innovation, and delivering solutions that keep the world connected, efficiently and securely.

Our Core Values

Our values define who we are as a team and how we approach our work every day:

  • Respect: We believe in fostering a respectful environment where we value each other's perspectives and contributions. We maintain a deep respect for our colleagues, our open-source community, and our clients, ensuring that all interactions are guided by understanding, professionalism, and empathy.
  • Responsibility: Trust is the foundation of our success. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of honesty, dependability, and accountability. Whether delivering on a commitment to a client or collaborating with a team member, we take responsibility for our actions and their impact.
  • Improvement: We are driven by a relentless desire to improve - ourselves, our products, and the world of networking. Continuous learning, innovation, and refining our processes are key to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
  • Contentment: At VyOS Networks, we believe that work should inspire and fulfill. We create an environment where people are excited to collaborate, share ideas, and find joy in solving real-world problems. We aim to inspire others while finding inspiration in the work we do.

jobs.excerpt: About Us:OncoveryCare is an early-stage virtual healthcare company committed to fundamentally rethinking and transforming the landscape of physical and mental healthcare for cancer survivors.
jobs.description:
About Us:

OncoveryCare is an early-stage virtual healthcare company committed to fundamentally rethinking and transforming the landscape of physical and mental healthcare for cancer survivors. Our team is composed of cancer survivors, clinicians, and experts in cutting-edge healthcare delivery. We believe that world class care after a cancer diagnosis shouldn’t end when treatment is over, and we provide an innovative, evidence-based approach to deliver patient-centered, whole-person support for survivors throughout the cancer journey.

Our vision is a world where living beyond cancer isn’t just “surviving”—it’s thriving.

A few tidbits about cancer survivorship:

  • There are over 18 million cancer survivors in the United States today—and that number is expected to grow to 26 million by 2040
  • Cancer survivors experience a range of physical and mental health side effects from treatment
  • Survivorship starts at the moment of diagnosis and continues post-treatment—we are starting in the “transitions of care” phase post-treatment, when there is often not a specialized team to take over caring for the survivor moving forward

Our Guiding Principles:

  • By survivors, for survivors: We build the survivor voice and experience into all that we do
  • Clinical integrity and rigor: We prioritize evidence-based approaches and an integrated team to deliver the highest-quality care
  • Trauma-informed care: We “meet survivors where they are” and respect their lived experience
  • Changing the status quo: We are committed to radically reinventing how cancer survivorship care is designed, delivered, and experienced
  • Transparency & inclusivity: Building a new frontier of cancer care is both hard and rewarding—everyone has a role to play, and fostering a positive and open team culture is our priority

About the Role:

OncoveryCare uses a novel Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) to integrate psychiatric expertise directly into survivorship care, so that our multidisciplinary team—survivorship MDs, NPs, and behavioral health clinicians—can identify and treat common mental health conditions earlier and more effectively. As our Consulting Psychiatrist, you will be a core part of this model: providing systematic, registry-based caseload review, advising our treating providers on evidence-based medication and treatment strategies, and building the clinical judgment of our team so that more survivors get access to behavioral health support.

Candidates must hold an active, unrestricted psychiatric license and board certification. Licensure in New York is preferred.

What You’ll Do:

  • Structured Case Review (SCR): Meet weekly with our Behavioral Health Clinician(s) to systematically review a registry of patients, prioritizing those who are new to the caseload, clinically complex, or not improving as expected
  • Treatment Recommendations: Advise our survivorship medical providers on treatment strategies, tailored to the unique comorbidities and treatment histories of cancer survivors, including medication management when clinically indicated
  • Ad Hoc Consultation: Be available for occasional, timely consultation on complex or urgent patient situations flagged by the care team
  • Team Education: Deliver ongoing education to our behavioral health clinicians, NPs, and MDs on recognizing and managing psychiatric conditions common in cancer survivorship—treatment-related depression and anxiety, PTSD, cognitive changes, grief, and Fear of Cancer Recurrence
  • Documentation: Document consultation recommendations in OncoveryCare's registry/EMR in a timely manner, consistent with CoCM documentation standards

How You’ll Thrive:

  • Within the first 90 days, you will onboard with our clinical leadership and care team, become familiar with OncoveryCare's registry and documentation tools, and begin conducting structured case reviews with our behavioral health clinician(s).
  • Within the first year, you will have established a strong working rhythm with our care team, developed a nuanced understanding of the psychiatric needs specific to cancer survivors, and contributed meaningfully to the evolution of our CoCM protocols.
  • Long-term growth opportunity: As OncoveryCare scales across new markets and partner sites, you will have the opportunity to help define what psychiatric consultation looks like for cancer survivorship care nationally,

What You Will Need:

  • Board certification in Psychiatry (MD or DO)
  • Active, unrestricted medical license
  • Minimum 3 years of post-residency clinical experience
  • Experience with, or strong interest in, psycho-oncology, consultation-liaison psychiatry, or integrated/collaborative care models
  • Proficiency with evidence-based treatment of common psychiatric conditions, including navigating complex comorbid medical conditions and treatment interactions relevant to oncology (e.g., chemotherapy, endocrine therapy)
  • Familiarity with measurement-based care tools (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5)
  • Comfort working in a consultative capacity—advising treating providers through registry review rather than direct patient encounters
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex clinical presentations into clear, actionable recommendations
  • Availability for a part-time weekly commitment, with flexibility to scale as our patient panel grows

Who You Are:

  • Strong clinical judgment. You can quickly synthesize psychiatric and general medical history to formulate clear, evidence-based recommendations
  • Patient centric. You are deeply committed to patient care and impact
  • High EQ. You communicate complex psychiatric reasoning in a way that's accessible and actionable for non-psychiatric providers
  • Startup oriented: You're comfortable working in a fast-paced, early-stage environment and helping build a program from the ground up
  • Growth Mindset. You actively look for ways to improve care protocols and enjoy sharing insights with clinical leadership
  • Forward thinking. You're excited by the potential of integrated, tech-enabled psychiatric care and by the specific challenge of survivorship mental health

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Competitive hourly consulting rate, commensurate with experience and subspecialty expertise
  • Fully remote
  • Malpractice/professional liability coverage related to consultation activities

der moment

Seit 2018 hat Jurafuchs Hunderttausende Jurastudierende und Referendare beim Lernen begleitet und ist heute die führende Lernplattform für juristische Bildung im deutschsprachigen Raum. Mit Bwlfuchs bauen wir gerade eine zweite Marke für Wirtschafts- und BWL-Studierende auf und beide sollen den gleichen visuellen Anspruch haben. Design ist für uns kein Nice-to-have, sondern der Ort, an dem unsere Marken jeden Tag entstehen und genau deshalb bauen wir dafür jetzt ein eigenes In-House Design-Team auf, das eng mit unserem Marketing- und Product-Design-Team zusammenarbeitet, statt Design punktuell nebenbei mitlaufen zu lassen.

Dafür suchen wir jemanden, der unseren Marken in jedem Post, jedem Template, jeder Kampagne ein Gesicht gibt mit einem Auge für Details und einem Portfolio, das zeigt, dass du das schon kannst.

deine mission

Du gibst unseren Marken – Jurafuchs und Bwlfuchs – ein Gesicht: in jedem Post, jedem Template, jeder Kampagne. Design und Marketing sind für dich keine getrennten Welten, sondern eine gemeinsame Baustelle.

woran du bei uns arbeitest

Du bist Teil unseres In-House Design-Teams und arbeitest eng mit unseren Marketing Managern und Product Designern zusammen, um unsere Marken – Jurafuchs und Bwlfuchs – über alle Kanäle hinweg sichtbar zu machen – von schnellem Social Content bis zu durchdachter Markenarbeit. Das zeigt sich zum Beispiel darin, dass:

  • Print- und Digital-Assets entstehen, die zu unserer Design Language passen – von Social-Media-Visuals über Landingpages bis zu Kampagnen-Grafiken

  • Bwlfuchs als zweite Marke im gleichen Qualitätsanspruch wie Jurafuchs visuell mit aufgebaut wird

  • unsere Brand Guidelines und Visual Identity kontinuierlich weiterentwickelt und im Alltag konsequent angewendet werden

  • Social-Media-Assets wie Posts, Stories, Animationen und Kampagnen-Grafiken entstehen, die auf jeden Kanal zugeschnitten sind und trotzdem unverkennbar nach Jurafuchs aussehen

  • Landingpages, Web-Content und digitale Marketingmaterialien entstehen, die unsere Kampagnen visuell tragen

  • Infografiken und Layouts komplexe Inhalte klar und verständlich machen – digital wie in Print

  • Templates entstehen, die das Team wiederverwenden kann, statt jedes Mal von Null zu starten

  • unsere Marketing-Websites, die wir mit Framer und KI-Tools wie Claude umsetzen, visuell mitgestaltet und gepflegt werden

wer du bist

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung in einer vergleichbaren Design-Rolle mit und hast ein Portfolio, das zeigt, dass du in Creative Principles und Design Language denkst.

  • Du bist sicher im Umgang mit der Adobe Creative Suite, insbesondere Illustrator, InDesign und Photoshop.

  • Du hast ein starkes Gespür für Gestaltung, Typografie und Komposition.

  • Idealerweise hast du bereits mit AI-Tools im Design-Workflow gearbeitet und Erfahrung in der Erstellung von Social-Media-Assets gesammelt.

  • Du sprichst Deutsch mindestens auf C1-Niveau und fühlst dich sicher im Umgang mit deutschen Texten und Copywriting.

  • Du bewegst dich mühelos zwischen schnellem Social-Content und durchdachter Markenarbeit, ohne dass die Qualität leidet auch wenn mehrere Projekte gleichzeitig laufen.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenständig und bringst eigene Ideen ein, statt nur Briefings abzuarbeiten.

was du wissen solltest

Du triffst nicht auf eine leere Struktur: Es gibt ein bestehendes Marketing- und Produkt-Team, mit dem du eng zusammenarbeitest. Die In-House-Design-Funktion selbst baust du von Anfang an mit auf – du entscheidest viel selbst, wie Assets aussehen, wie Templates strukturiert sind und wo unsere Visual Identity als nächstes hingeht.

Die Rolle ist bewusst breit angelegt: Du bewegst dich zwischen schnellem Social-Content und größeren Marken-Projekten, je nachdem, was gerade am meisten zählt.

was dich erwartet

Build Fast: Jede Woche neue Features, kurze Entscheidungswege und eine AI-First Mentalität.

Work Your Way: 100 % remote, flexible Arbeitszeiten und Fokus auf Ergebnisse statt Präsenz.

One Team: Radical Candor, Eigenverantwortung und zero Tolerance für Ego-Show. 2× im Jahr treffen wir uns zu Teamretreats in Europa.

Why We Exist: Wir glauben, dass der Zugang zu juristischer Bildung eine Frage von gesellschaftlicher & rechtsstaatlicher Relevanz ist. Deshalb machen wir juristische Bildung zugänglicher, wirksamer und relevanter.

jobs.description:
Intelligence Center X is Siemens' platform for the agentic enterprise

The next wave of enterprise software isn't about writing more code — it's about giving organizations the tools to combine trusted data, AI, and applications into systems that can reason and act on their own. Intelligence Center X delivers that today, through five capabilities — an Enterprise Knowledge Graph, AI/ML, agentic application development, orchestration, and governance — that together move enterprises from static software to intelligent, autonomous systems.

For the customers we serve, that shift shows up in very concrete ways: engineers and data leaders who can finally find and trust the data buried across decades of enterprise systems; teams that go from idea to working application in days instead of quarters; and AI initiatives that move out of pilot purgatory and into production because the underlying data and governance can actually support them. Whether you're building this platform, proving its value to customers, or bringing it to market through our partner ecosystem, your work directly drives those outcomes for some of the most complex organizations in the world.

This is one of the most ambitious enterprise AI platforms in the market — built on decades of deep domain expertise across industries as varied as manufacturing, banking, insurance, financial services, and healthcare, and already running in production at real scale for organizations with some of the most demanding data and compliance requirements in the world. If you want to work at the intersection of enterprise AI, knowledge graphs, and agentic applications — with real customers and real production stakes, across nearly every major industry — this is where that work is happening.

Solution Architect

Position Overview

The Solution Architect is the technical leader for customer engagements delivered by Siemens Professional Services. Working across industries and a broad portfolio that includes Intelligence Center X (ICX), SLC, Mendix, and other Siemens Digital Industries Software offerings, this role translates business outcomes and process needs into secure, scalable, and supportable solution architectures.

The role leads solution definition from discovery through design, build, integration, validation, deployment, and transition. The Solution Architect governs the integrity of the end-to-end solution, aligns customer and delivery teams around clear architectural decisions, and ensures that functional and non-functional requirements are implemented using Siemens methods, standard capabilities, and reusable patterns wherever practical.

Success requires hands-on architecture leadership, strong customer communication, disciplined technical governance, and the ability to orchestrate applications, data, AI, integrations, and workflows into a coherent solution that can be operated and expanded over time.

Key Responsibilities

1. Discovery and Solution Definition

  • Lead technical discovery workshops to understand customer processes, business outcomes, users, data, systems, constraints, and measures of success.
  • Partner with the Engagement Manager, Sales, Presales, and customer stakeholders to convert value hypotheses and high-level scope into an executable solution approach.
  • Define the end-to-end architecture across relevant Siemens and customer capabilities, including applications, data, integrations, AI, workflow, identity, security, and operational considerations.
  • Establish the solution vision, architecture principles, major design decisions, assumptions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
  • Identify where standard product capabilities, configuration, extension, or custom development should be used, favoring maintainable and upgradeable patterns.
  • Create solution-definition deliverables that provide sufficient clarity for estimation, planning, build, testing, deployment, and support.

2. Architecture and Design Governance

  • Own the technical integrity and coherence of the complete solution, including components delivered by Siemens, customers, partners, and distributed teams.
  • Author and govern architecture documents, functional and technical specifications, interface designs, data models, decision records, and implementation guidance.
  • Define and validate non-functional requirements such as security, performance, scalability, availability, traceability, usability, and supportability.
  • Lead design reviews and ensure implementation decisions remain aligned with the approved architecture, scope, and customer outcomes.
  • Manage technical debt and deviations by documenting rationale, impact, risk, mitigation, and required approvals.
  • Maintain traceability from requirements and business processes through design, configuration, integration, testing, and acceptance.
  • Ensure the architecture supports sustainable operations, future roadmap needs, and appropriate reuse across releases or use cases.

3. Technical Delivery Leadership

  • Provide day-to-day technical direction to consultants, developers, data and AI specialists, integration resources, QA teams, and partners.
  • Decompose the solution into implementable work packages and support the Project Manager with estimates, sequencing, dependencies, and detailed work breakdown structures.
  • Clarify design intent, resolve technical ambiguity, and remove blockers so distributed teams can execute efficiently.
  • Validate that configured, extended, and integrated components implement the approved design and meet quality expectations.
  • Coordinate technical activities across build, integration, data migration, testing, deployment, and transition to operations.
  • Lead technical triage and root-cause analysis for complex cross-product or cross-domain issues, ensuring decisions and corrective actions are documented.
  • Support release readiness, cutover planning, hypercare, and knowledge transfer from an architecture perspective.

4. Customer and Stakeholder Leadership

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor to the customer during delivery, communicating architecture choices, tradeoffs, risks, and implications clearly.
  • Guide customers toward Siemens best practices and standard capabilities while ensuring legitimate business and technical needs are addressed.
  • Facilitate decisions across business, IT, security, architecture, and operational stakeholders when priorities or constraints conflict.
  • Proactively manage customer expectations related to feasibility, scope, dependencies, quality, and technical risk.
  • Present solution status, design decisions, and technical issues to project governance forums and executive stakeholders at the appropriate level of detail.
