jobs.title: PR & Media Hacker
jobs.excerpt: “For every person joining us for any position, there is a path and an opportunity to reach an executive role and become a company partner.
jobs.description:
“For every person joining us for any position, there is a path and an opportunity to reach an executive role and become a company partner.”
Antons Sapriko, Company Founder

How to become a PR & Media Hacker at scandiweb?

We are a very inclusive company with colleagues from over 30 countries across all continents. We welcome people from all walks of life who can complete a practical test by showing how they think, create stories, and turn an ordinary business topic into something people want to discuss.
This is not a traditional PR position where your main responsibility is to prepare press releases, upload them to distribution platforms, and send the same pitch to a long media list. We are looking for someone who knows how to direct people's attention.
Your job will be to find the tension, consequence, opponent, proof, or human angle that turns it into a story worth sharing.
Sometimes the story already exists and needs to be discovered. Sometimes you will help create the real event, benchmark, public challenge, experiment, debate, collaboration, or campaign that gives the media a reason to cover it.
We welcome previous experience in PR, journalism, communications, creative agencies, content, startups, or growth marketing. However, the strongest evidence of your ability will be how you approach the practical tasks.
We value your ability to deliver results, your curiosity, your persistence, and your openness to learn from feedback. Continuous learning and acting on feedback are among our core organizational values.

What are the responsibilities of a PR & Media Hacker?

As a PR & Media Hacker at scandiweb, your main responsibility will be to create public attention around scandiweb, internal ventures, company developments, and selected client projects.
You will work closely with company founders and business leaders to identify stories that deserve public attention. You will not wait for someone to hand you a finished announcement. You will proactively search for opportunities, develop the angle, shape the campaign, collect the proof, and bring the story to the right audience.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Finding PR opportunities inside scandiweb (e.g., projects, client work, internal discussions, product development, research, technical achievements, market changes, etc)
  • Turning complex or seemingly ordinary topics into stories worth sharing with a strong headline, tension, consequence, and reason for people to care;
  • Developing creative PR campaigns and stunts and making people speak about it;
  • Creating real newsworthy moments when a strong story does not yet exist, rather than just waiting for them to appear;
  • Building several media angles around the same core event for different audiences;
  • Researching journalists, editors, newsletter writers, podcasters, creators, analysts, and industry communities that are relevant to each story;
  • Preparing personalized pitches and reaching out directly through email, social media, calls, introductions, events, and other appropriate channels;
  • Building long-term relationships with media professionals by understanding what they cover and bringing them useful, timely, and credible stories;
  • Coordinating interviews, expert comments, supporting data, visuals, demonstrations, customer evidence, and spokesperson preparation;
  • Working with content, design, video, data, and development teams to create the materials needed to prove and distribute a story;
  • Monitoring public conversations, competitor activity, industry news, and cultural trends to identify moments when scandiweb can contribute a relevant point of view;
  • Responding quickly when an unexpected media opportunity appears and coordinating the required internal contributors;
  • Using AI and research tools to monitor media, find patterns, identify relevant contacts, develop angles, and improve outreach without turning communication into automated spam;
  • Measuring campaign results, documenting what worked, and improving future campaigns based on actual media response and business impact.
The number of press releases produced will not measure success in this role.
It will be measured by the quality and relevance of earned media coverage, the conversations your campaigns create, the relationships you build, the attention generated among the right audiences, and the business opportunities supported by your work.

What do we expect from you?

We are looking for a curious, persistent, and highly proactive person who naturally looks for the story behind what is happening.
You may come from PR, journalism, media, content, communications, creative strategy, startup marketing, or another relevant background. A traditional PR career can come in handy. Still, you should be able to demonstrate that you have previously attracted attention, earned coverage, built an audience, or created public interest around an idea.
The following qualities will help you succeed in the role:
  • Strong news judgment and the ability to understand why one story gets covered while another is ignored;
  • The ability to find a compelling angle in technical, commercial, or otherwise ordinary information;
  • Excellent headline, pitch, and short-form writing skills;
  • Confident written and spoken English, as you will be working with international media and clients;
  • The ability to understand technical and business topics and explain them in simple language;
  • A proactive attitude and willingness to contact people directly rather than waiting for inbound interest;
  • Persistence when pitches are ignored, rejected, or require several attempts before receiving a response;
  • Comfort working with incomplete information and developing a campaign while the underlying project is still evolving;
  • The ability to manage several stories, stakeholders, and deadlines at the same time;
  • Confidence when communicating with founders, executives, technical experts, clients, journalists, and creators;
  • The ability to work independently, make decisions, and take responsibility for campaign outcomes;
  • Curiosity about media, business, technology, eCommerce, culture, and the reasons people share information;

jobs.title: Chief Marketing Officer
jobs.excerpt: Real opportunities.  Real impact.  Your career, redefined.
jobs.description:
Real opportunities. Real impact. Your career, redefined.

(NOTE: A human reviews every application at Oceans, so please apply for only one position and only once a year—if you're a better fit for another role, we’ll route your application accordingly and if we’re not quite ready for you, we’ll reach back out later.)

At Oceans, we help the best and brightest of Sri Lanka to take advantage of opportunities that otherwise wouldn’t be available to them, while supporting entrepreneurs around the world. Our community (we call them Divers) don’t do surface work—they go deep to solve complex challenges and make a real impact. And in doing so, they support bold ideas, expand their skills, broaden their expertise, and grow their careers, all without having to leave family and friends.

As the Chief Marketing Officer, you will own the marketing and growth strategy for an early-stage direct-to-consumer subscription business, helping build the brand, acquisition engine, and go-to-market model from the ground up. You'll work closely with the founders and leadership team to shape market positioning, drive subscriber growth, build creator and community-led acquisition, strengthen retention and customer lifetime value, and establish the marketing foundation required to scale across markets.

This is a leadership role with a distinctly hands-on mandate. Rather than setting strategy and delegating execution to a large team, you'll be expected to determine where and how the business should grow, then roll up your sleeves to build the campaigns, partnerships, systems, processes, and measurement frameworks that bring that strategy to life. As the function matures, you'll evolve from individual execution into building and leading the broader marketing organization.

Here's how you'll make an impact:

Accountability

Marketing Strategy & Leadership

  • Own the overall marketing strategy and growth agenda in partnership with the founders and leadership team.
  • Translate company goals into clear marketing priorities, channel strategies, investment decisions, and measurable outcomes.
  • Establish the marketing vision, operating rhythm, and strategic roadmap for the business.
  • Balance long-term brand building with near-term subscriber acquisition and commercial performance.
  • Identify the capabilities, resources, and investments required to support the company's growth trajectory.
  • Serve as the senior marketing voice in company-wide strategic and commercial decisions.

Brand Strategy & Positioning

  • Own and evolve the brand positioning, voice, messaging, and consumer narrative.
  • Build a differentiated premium brand within a trust-sensitive consumer category.
  • Translate the company's mission and value proposition into compelling consumer-facing messaging.
  • Establish messaging frameworks that can scale across channels and geographic markets.
  • Maintain consistency across paid, organic, creator, lifecycle, community, and customer touchpoints.
  • Ensure brand development strengthens both customer trust and commercial performance.

Subscriber Acquisition & Growth

  • Own the customer acquisition strategy across paid, organic, creator-led, affiliate, and community channels.
  • Determine channel priorities and allocate marketing investment based on performance, growth potential, and customer economics.
  • Own subscriber acquisition performance and continuously improve customer acquisition economics.
  • Identify, test, and validate new growth opportunities and channels.
  • Develop a repeatable acquisition model that can support expansion into additional markets.
  • Connect acquisition performance to downstream retention, customer quality, and lifetime value.

Creator, Influencer & Community Growth

  • Build the creator and influencer growth strategy from the ground up.
  • Identify and evaluate creators who align with the brand and target customer.
  • Develop creator partnerships, affiliate relationships, campaigns, and measurement frameworks.
  • Personally manage key creator relationships and outreach during the early stages of the function.
  • Establish repeatable systems for sourcing, briefing, tracking, and evaluating creator performance.
  • Develop creator and community activity into a meaningful acquisition and retention channel rather than treating it solely as brand awareness.

Paid Acquisition

  • Own the strategic direction and investment approach across relevant paid acquisition channels.
  • Evaluate channel allocation, acquisition economics, and growth opportunities.
  • Oversee campaign setup, creative requirements, QA, testing, and optimization.
  • Monitor CAC, ROAS, subscriber conversion, and downstream customer quality.
  • Use performance data to determine where to increase, reduce, or redirect marketing investment.
  • Work with internal or external specialists where appropriate while retaining executive accountability for results.

Lifecycle, Retention & Customer Value

  • Own the customer lifecycle strategy across onboarding, engagement, retention, churn prevention, and win-back.
  • Develop email and SMS programs using platforms such as Klaviyo.
  • Build subscriber onboarding and nurture journeys that strengthen customer relationships.
  • Develop retention, churn reduction, referral, and loyalty initiatives.
  • Use behavioral and lifecycle segmentation to improve customer engagement.
  • Increase repeat purchase, retention, and subscriber lifetime value.
  • Establish a structured test-and-learn approach to customer lifecycle performance.

Conversion & Customer Journey

  • Own the customer journey from initial acquisition through subscription and ongoing engagement.
  • Identify friction across landing pages, offers, checkout, and subscription flows.
  • Develop and prioritize conversion improvements based on customer and performance data.
  • Work across the Shopify and subscription technology stack to improve the purchase experience.
  • Ensure acquisition investment translates into high-quality customers and sustainable subscription growth.
  • Build a culture of continuous experimentation across the customer funnel.

Marketing Analytics & Commercial Performance

  • Establish the measurement framework for the marketing function and broader growth engine.
  • Track CAC, LTV, subscriber conversion, retention, churn, ROAS, and channel performance.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of paid, organic, creator, lifecycle, and community programs.
  • Translate marketing performance into clear commercial recommendations and investment decisions.
  • Identify trends, opportunities, and risks across the customer funnel.
  • Provide leadership with clear visibility into marketing performance, efficiency, and growth potential.

Marketing Operations & Execution

  • Build the operating infrastructure required for a high-performing marketing function.
  • Establish campaign calendars, workflows, processes, timelines, QA standards, and reporting rhythms.
  • Coordinate content and campaign production across internal and external resources.
  • Maintain oversight of the Shopify, subscription, CRM, and broader marketing technology ecosystem.
  • Ensure campaigns and initiatives launch accurately, efficiently, and on schedule.
  • Build scalable processes that reduce reliance on founder-driven or ad hoc execution.
  • Remain directly involved in campaign development, optimization, reporting, and execution while the function is lean.

Multi-Market GTM & Function Building

  • Develop a repeatable marketing and go-to-market playbook for geographic expansion.
  • Determine which acquisition, community, brand, and lifecycle approaches can be replicated across markets.
  • Adapt positioning, messaging, and channel strategies where market or regulatory differences require it.
  • Establish the systems, processes, and capabilities needed to scale the marketing function.
  • Identify future marketing leadership and specialist hiring needs.
  • Build and lead a high-performing marketing team as the business grows.
  • Evolve the marketing organization from a lean, hands-on function into a scalable growth engine.

Colleagues

You'll work closely with the company's founders and leadership team, acting as the senior marketing owner across brand, growth, acquisition, retention, and go-to-market strategy. You'll also coordinate with creators, influencers, marketing specialists, external partners, and other resources supporting growth. As the function develops, you'll be responsible for building the team and creating an environment where marketing can scale effectively.

At Oceans Talent, you'll also receive guidance and support from your Operations Manager, who will help you succeed in the role and ensure that you're continuously growing and developing in your career.

Skills and Qualifications

As a Chief Marketing Officer, your vertical focus will be on marketing strategy, brand leadership, DTC growth, and commercial performance, while your horizontal focus will include acquisition, lifecycle marketing, analytics, creator growth, conversion optimization, marketing operations, GTM, and AI-enabled execution.

  • Experience: 8+ years of experience across growth marketing, brand marketing, marketing leadership, or related disciplines, with significant ownership of acquisition, retention, and commercial outcomes.
  • Executive Marketing Leadership: Demonstrated ability to own marketing strategy, make independent investment decisions, and connect marketing activity to broader business objectives.
  • DTC & Subscription Growth: Strong experience building and scaling direct-to-consumer or subscription growth programs.
  • Acquisition: Demonstrated experience across both paid and organic acquisition, with a strong understanding of channel economics.
  • Lifecycle Marketing: Hands-on experience developing email, SMS, retention, churn reduction, referral, loyalty, and LTV programs.
  • Creator & Influencer Growth: Proven experience building or scaling creator, influencer, affiliate, or community-led acquisition programs.
  • Brand Strategy: Strong judgment in positioning, messaging, voice, and premium consumer brand development.
  • Marketing Analytics: Strong understanding of CAC, LTV, retention, churn, ROAS, conversion, and channel performance, with the ability to turn data into commercial decisions.
  • Go-to-Market: Experience developing repeatable GTM strategies and scaling marketing across multiple markets or customer segments.
  • Marketing Operations: Ability to build the systems, processes, workflows, and infrastructure required to scale a marketing function from a relatively blank slate.
  • Hands-On Execution: Comfortable personally building, managing, analyzing, and optimizing marketing programs while the function remains lean.
  • Team Building: Ability to identify future capabilities, hire effectively, and develop a high-performing marketing team as the business scales.
  • Startup & Build-from-Zero Experience: Comfortable operating with ambiguity, limited infrastructure, and minimal hand-holding.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate clearly across strategic, creative, analytical, operational, and executive contexts.
  • AI Fluency: Strong proficiency with AI tools and willingness to incorporate tools such as Claude into research, analysis, campaign development, content workflows, and marketing operations.

During the interview process, you'll have the opportunity to showcase your skills in the following areas:

  • Marketing Strategy & Executive Leadership: Your ability to develop and own a marketing strategy, set priorities, lead a marketing function, and connect marketing activity to broader business goals.
  • DTC Growth & Customer Acquisition: Your ability to build and optimize acquisition strategies across paid, organic, and other growth channels while balancing customer acquisition costs, conversion, and sustainable growth.
  • Brand Strategy & Positioning: Your ability to shape a distinctive brand, translate positioning into effective marketing, and ensure consistency across channels, audiences, and customer touchpoints.
  • Creator, Influencer & Community Growth: Your ability to develop creator and influencer partnerships, build engaged communities, and turn these relationships into meaningful and measurable growth.
  • Lifecycle, Retention & Customer Value: Your ability to develop lifecycle strategies that improve engagement, retention, conversion, and customer lifetime value across the customer journey.
  • Marketing Analytics, Commercial Decision-Making & Execution: Your ability to use marketing and commercial data to make decisions, identify opportunities, prioritize resources, and remain hands-on in executing and improving marketing initiatives.

Diversity of experience is core to Oceans. You are expected to work inclusively with individuals from a variety of backgrounds, ensuring that both personal and collective dignity are supported.

Role Specifications

This is a remote role, where you will be expected to work a split shift with some overlap with our client’s time zone. You will, however, be expected to be present for in-person training programs during your first 3.5 weeks with us. During the offer process, we’ll share more information about our benefits and compensation philosophy, considering both market trends and individual factors.

About Oceans

At Oceans Talent, we connect the world’s top talent with visionary companies building what’s next. Here, you’re not just stepping into another role — you’re joining a team that values individuality, ambition, and growth without limits. Unique, like you.

We’re always excited to share more about our journey, where we’re headed, and how you can grow with us throughout the interview process.

Want to learn more about our recruitment process, what to expect from interviews, and possible outcomes? Check out [The Dive].

jobs.title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
jobs.excerpt: Who we areMoniepoint Inc.  is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

Why South Africa

South Africa has one of the strongest engineering communities anywhere in the world, and we are deliberately growing our technology organisation in the country. We already have several team members based here. The work is fully remote, and the mission we are working on is a good deal closer to home than it is for our teams elsewhere.

So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in South Africa.

About The Role

Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people.

Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale.

The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve.

This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader.

Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs.

You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes:

  • Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end.
  • Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority.
  • Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents.
  • Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales.
  • Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour.
  • Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives.
  • Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned.
  • Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience.
  • Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands.
  • Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them.

Who You Are

  • Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role.
  • Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs.
  • Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them.
  • At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team.
  • Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead.
  • 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases.
  • Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits.
  • Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers.
  • Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work.
  • Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required.
  • Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement.

Cultural Alignment

As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.

  • Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.
  • Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.
  • Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.
  • Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early.
  • Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders.
  • No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes.
  • Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not.
  • Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.

What Success Looks Like In The Role

  • The existing cashback product performing measurably better — faster, more reliable, and more compelling to customers.
  • A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped.
  • A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle.
  • An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers.
  • Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base.
  • Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units.

Why Join Us

  • A rare blank page. The platform exists, but almost everything it could become is still ahead of it, and you will define what that is.
  • Direct influence on retention across a base of roughly 23 million users, at one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa.
  • Full autonomy as the CTO of your domain, with the backing to build the organisation you think the problem needs.
  • Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals.

What To Expect In The Hiring Process

  • 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers.
  • 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes.
  • 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business.
  • 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager).

Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

Location: Poland, remote

Tidio is the customer service platform that aligns AI and people, so businesses can scale without losing trust or the human touch. Our goal is to help entrepreneurs grow by making customer service more efficient while keeping it helpful.

Working at Tidio means impacting thousands of companies and millions of their users. But our clients are not the only ones who can grow with us. By joining Tidio, you can grow, too!

Lyro, one of our flagship AI products,is to customer service what Claude is to AI — a customer service platform that lets teams build, test, and deploy customer service agents anywhere.

A few facts about us:

  • Our product is one of the world's leading AI customer service solutions, and our goal is to become no. 1

  • We are among the Top 50 AI and Customer Service Products in G2’s Best Software Awards 2024.

  • We currently rate at 4.7/5 in both Shopify and G2.

  • Our ML team was among the first in the world to launch an AI agent (Lyro) for customer service!

  • Every month, our widget is viewed by 350 million unique users, which is 4% of the global population.

  • Currently, we hire over 150 fantastic people.

By joining Tidio as Head of Finance, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how finance supports a fast-growing SaaS business — not just keep the numbers in order. You won’t be starting from scratch: our core finance processes are already in place, giving you the space to focus on business partnering, deeper analysis, and helping the company make better decisions. With no CFO in our structure, you’ll be a key finance partner to the business and C-level, turning financial insights into recommendations and helping shape decisions across the company.

You’ll join our six-person Finance & Operations team and directly manage a three-person team covering controlling and accounting, while working closely with the wider organization on budgeting, cash flow, business performance, and strategic initiatives. Reporting directly to our Chief of Staff, you’ll combine hands-on financial expertise with the ability to zoom out, understand the business, challenge assumptions, and advise on what we should do next.

As the Head of Finance, you will:

  • Act as a strategic finance partner to C-level and business leaders, bringing financial perspective to key decisions, challenging assumptions, and turning data into clear recommendations.

  • Manage a three-person team covering controlling and accounting, ensuring high-quality financial operations and clear ownership across the function.

  • Own budgeting and forecasting, working closely with teams across the organization to understand their plans, challenge assumptions, and ensure resources are allocated effectively.

  • Develop financial reporting around key SaaS metrics and use it to help the business understand performance, identify inefficiencies, and make better decisions.

  • Assess the profitability and financial impact of growth and development initiatives, providing recommendations on where and how to invest.

  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and recommend and implement actions to improve cost efficiency, partnering with other teams to drive sustainable improvements.

  • Own cash flow management and FX hedging, including cash flow forecasting, cash operations, and FX risk management.

  • Partner with the Tax Manager on tax-related projects and decisions, contributing financial and business perspective and ensuring tax considerations are properly reflected in broader financial decisions.

  • Maintain accounting structures across the group and optimize them when needed.

  • Oversee the capitalization of intangible assets (WNIP) and ensure it is handled appropriately from an accounting perspective.

Requirements

You are the perfect fit if you have:

  • At least 3 years of experience as a Head of Finance or in a similar senior finance role working in fast-scaling companies.

  • Strong business partnering experience, with a track record of working closely with upper management across the organization and bringing financial perspective to business decisions.

  • Strategic thinking and strong decision-making skills, with the ability to be a sparring partner to C-level and provide clear, well-reasoned recommendations.

  • A hands-on mindset and a willingness to get into the details, while also being able to step back, see the bigger picture, and recommend practical solutions.

  • Solid experience in budgeting, forecasting, and KPI management, with the ability to turn financial data into meaningful business insights.

  • Strong analytical and financial modelling skills, including building and working with forecasting models.

  • Very good knowledge of cash management and accounting.

  • A good understanding of statutory tax requirements in Poland, with enough tax awareness to engage in meaningful discussions with the Tax Manager.

  • Good knowledge of GAAP and IFRS.

  • Fluent English for day-to-day business and finance communication.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience in the SaaS industry.

  • Experience with payment processor reconciliations.

  • Familiarity with US GAAP.

We would like to offer you:

  • Be part of a Polish-founded company operating globally at the forefront of AI-powered customer service — our ML team was among the first in the world to launch an AI agent (Lyro) for customer service.

  • A unique opportunity to build on a strong finance foundation and help take the business to the next level — from keeping the numbers right to driving growth, while being a true strategic partner to C-level and investors.

  • A high-impact role with real ownership, where your recommendations can shape major strategic decisions and have a lasting impact on the business.

  • A flat internal structure, with plenty of space to make decisions, challenge the status quo, and turn your ideas into action.

  • Work closely with C-level and business leaders who are driven by results, focused on creating real value, and passionate about building products that are meaningful to our customers and the market.

On top of that

  • ESOP — the opportunity to become a shareholder in Tidio and benefit from the company’s long-term success.

  • Unlimited paid time off, plus local bank holidays.

  • Remote or hybrid work model from our Warsaw/Szczecin office.

  • Sport & wellness benefit — no extra charge.

  • Private medical care — no extra charge.

  • Mental well-being program, including individual therapy sessions and resources for employees.

  • Free access to one of the most popular e-book and audiobook services.

  • Regular social events, including company-wide offsites and team events.

  • Individual work tools — MacBook Pro, Dell monitor, JBL headphones, and the flexibility to tailor your setup to your needs.

What happens when you send your CV?

  • Video call with a recruiter about the position and the team.

  • Meeting the Hiring Manager

  • Recruitment Task

  • Meeting the team

Diversity Statement

One of Tidio’s core values is to play fair. Therefore, we treat all candidates equally. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status. This means recruitment and selection of talent to Tidio is only based on individual merit and qualifications directly related to professional competence.

JOB DESCRIPTION

RENEWAL RISK ENGINEER, [Management Liability]

Counterpart is an insurtech platform reimagining management and professional liability for the modern workplace. We believe that when businesses lead with clarity and confidence, they become more resilient, more innovative, and better prepared for what’s ahead. That’s why we built the first Agentic Insurance™ system — where advanced AI and deep insurance expertise come together to proactively assess, mitigate, and manage risk. Backed by A rated carriers and trusted by brokers nationwide, our platform helps small businesses grow with confidence. Join us in shaping a smarter future, helping businesses Do More With Less Risk®.

Counterpart is the place for people who want to build and use top-tier technology to improve insurance products and outcomes for small businesses. You will own real problems, work alongside the future leaders of this industry, and help build a company defining a category.

As a member of the risk engineering team, you will be responsible for the production of premium through proper risk analysis and effective distribution of our product. In collaboration with the engineering, design, data, and operations team, you will leverage your industry knowledge and broker relationships to develop management liability and professional liability insurance products that brokers are eager to promote to their clients.

AS A PRODUCTION FOCUSED RISK ENGINEER YOU WILL:

  • Provide quick and competitive quotes in alignment with distribution and market strategies.
  • Serve as a trusted partner to wholesale brokers by offering thoughtful underwriting guidance and responsive communication.

  • Represent Counterpart at broker meetings, industry conferences, and networking events.

jobs.description:
**Candidates must reside in Indonesia and have existing authorisation to work there**

About Us

Revalue is a carbon credit development platform focused on one of the planet’s most critical but complex challenges - seeing nature regenerated at a planetary scale.

Our mission is to design the most cutting-edge and trusted nature credits for our planet.

We are bringing together a world-class team - forestry experts, ecologists, applied AI scientists, software engineers, geospatial analysts, commercial specialists, economists, and more - to create the unique DNA required to reimagine nature credits.

About the role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our Engineering team within Platform Intelligence.

Platform Intelligence develops the data infrastructure, machine learning, geospatial pipelines, and technical systems behind Revalue's nature and carbon intelligence products. We turn scientific and analytical work into repeatable, reliable outputs: ingesting and validating Earth observation datasets, producing the analyses and baselines that underpin our carbon methodologies, designing monitoring systems, and running the cloud platform underneath.

This role is about moving from analytical and ML prototypes to production-grade systems. You will work closely with engineers, data scientists, and analysts to build data pipelines, productionise models, and improve reproducibility, making workflows maintainable, observable, and usable by others.

Some of the most important work is deciding what to build, how to model it, and where to draw boundaries. You will work with domain experts to make those decisions rather than simply implementing predefined specifications.

It is a hands-on role at the boundary between software engineering, data science, geospatial engineering, and cloud infrastructure. You will not be expected to lead scientific model development, but you will make sure the models run reliably in production.

Who we are looking for

Please note: Candidates must have existing authorisation to work in Indonesia.

A strong mid-level or senior individual contributor who can own delivery independently and turn complex technical workflows into stable production systems.

Key skills:

  • Strong software engineering background. Design, interface, contract, data and domain modeling.

  • Scientific programming background in any domain: geospatial, remote sensing, ML, signal/audio/vision, quant, simulation, bioinformatics. We care more about the pattern of experience rather than the specific domain: translating messy, abstract, real-world structures into correct data representations and transformations.

  • Comfortable across stacks and tools: generalist disposition, able to pick up new languages/frameworks as our needs shift.

  • Familiar with modern SWE practices and product-engineering: discovery, scoping, iterative and incremental delivery, comfortable operating in ambiguity.

Hard skills:

  • Good engineering practice: testing, code review, CI/CD, modular design, documentation.

  • Experience productionising analytical, data science, or ML workflows: turning exploratory code into reliable systems, with a working understanding of batch processing, reproducibility, monitoring, and deployment.

  • Day-to-day work is in scientific Python. However, we weigh fundamentals and data aptitude above prior Python experience: if you have done this kind of work in C++, Scala, … , that counts.

  • Cloud engineering experience, ideally on GCP and AWS, including designing and operating cloud-based data systems.

  • A pragmatic mindset: knowing when to build carefully, when to simplify, and when to avoid unnecessary complexity.

Soft skills:

  • Comfortable with high-visibility, shared-ownership, collaborative work: pairing on decisions, small trunk-based commits, and real-time feedback on work in progress.

  • Comfortable running discovery sessions with domain experts before building.

  • Strong communication, including presenting technical solutions to colleagues and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English.

Nice to have:

Experience in any of these would be valuable, though we do not expect all of them:

  • Geospatial data, raster/vector processing, Earth observation, or remote sensing.

  • Data quality checks, lineage, observability, or reproducibility tooling.

  • Full-stack experience: a backend and frontend you have maintained or owned.

  • Applying AI tools to improve engineering, developer, or analytical workflows.

  • Tools such as Docker, GitHub Actions, Dagster, Terraform, Postgres, DuckDB, Dask, xarray, rasterio, or geopandas.

  • Scientific computing, climate, nature, carbon, or environmental data.

  • Improving an existing platform, on a team where data scientists and analysts contribute code.

What you will do

  • Make design and data-modelling calls: what a manifest has to guarantee, where a boundary sits, what belongs in a shared library and what stays out, when to defer rather than build.

  • Build and maintain the geospatial data pipelines behind our datasets: syncing sources, validating and ingesting them, and exporting project-aligned outputs for analysis.

  • Turn notebooks, prototypes, and research code into tested, modular production code, and keep it that way as requirements change.

  • Productionise our modelling pipelines and the orchestration they run on: partitioned assets, schedules, and concurrency.

  • Make runs reproducible and observable: manifests, pinned dataset versions, deterministic outputs, and monitoring that tells us when something breaks.

  • Build new data and monitoring products, including proper cataloging for our datasets.

  • Performance tuning: profiling real runs, concurrency within memory bounds, and keeping runtime/cost predictable.

  • Work on the backend (Kotlin/Spring, Postgres) and frontend (React/Remix) where results reach customers.

  • Own cloud infrastructure in Terraform across GCP and AWS: batch jobs, storage, IAM, CI/CD, and alerting.

  • Run discovery with scientists and analysts.

  • Contribute to dev tooling: ship/release scripts, agent skills that encode our engineering procedures, and repo instructions.

What success looks like

In the first few months, you will get to know our platform, cloud setup, and data workflows, and start owning productionisation work. Over time you will help build clearer patterns, more reliable pipelines, and better reproducibility and monitoring.

You will be doing well if analyses are easier to run and repeat, if analysts and scientists depend less on manual processes, if pipelines are predictable in runtime and cost, and if fewer critical systems rely on one person to keep them moving.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to shape the future of nature-based climate finance

  • A mission-driven organisation with shared purpose, culture, and values

  • A diverse team of colleagues, partners and clients based all around the world

  • Meaningful equity in an early-stage startup with a growing and trusted brand

  • Flexible working environment with a team deeply committed to impact

  • Generously enhanced, gender-neutral parental leave policy

  • Wellbeing support, including company-funded access to therapy

🌱 If you’re ready to build our Engineering function and care about driving real impact - we’d love to meet you!

About Lokal

In 2018, we began with a WhatsApp group with a simple hypothesis: people in tier-2/3 towns weren’t really using the internet meaningfully yet. We believed that if we started with local content in their own language, they’d come back every day; once there was a habit and trust, that same space could naturally grow into classifieds and, eventually, something they used for almost everything online.This spark became Lokal. Our first instinct was to put everything in one place & one app - local updates, classifieds, jobs, matrimony and more. It worked, till it stopped working. Users gave us the insight - when one use case outweighs the others, everything else seems like noise. We listened. Like how Craigslist quietly seeded a generation of focused companies & marketplaces, we began unbundling and verticalising.

Today, Lokal is a house of focused apps, many products, one mission:
to connect Tier-2/3+ India to the Knowledge, opportunities, tools and experts they’ve always deserved.We now operate dozens of live apps across categories like:

Edutainment & Skill Learning – practical skills and learning in regional languages (GyanTV)
Matrimonial Matchmaking – hyperlocal, compatibility-first partner search (Lokal Matrimony)
Agri Consulting – farmer-first advisory in local languages (AgriLokal)
Local Jobs – blue- and grey-collar opportunities close to home (Lokal Jobs, Sahi Jobs)
Social & Community – Place to find & post social updates (Lokal app)
Emotional Well-being & Peer Support – safe spaces to talk and feel heard (Dostt & Eaze)
Astrology & Guidance – instant access to trusted Astrologers via chat and voice (AstroLokal)
Advisory Services – early bets in legal help, financial guidance, career counselling, and more

Under the hood, Lokal is a discovery and access platform: local-language internet + deep Bharat insight+ AI. When someone opens a product we’ve built, they don’t wade through clutter; they get a straight line to what they came for.This is the story new teammates walk into a company that started as a whatsapp group, became a family of focused apps, and kept one belief at the centre — access changes lives.We ship fast. We learn fast. We build for Bharat.We are backed by leading global and domestic investors including Y Combinator, Sony, Global Brain, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital

jobs.excerpt: At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease.
jobs.description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.

As Senior Product Manager, Fisheries, you will own the Fisheries product end to end, from strategy and roadmap through to first release and go-to-market. Working closely with the Lead Product Manager – Maritime & Logistics, you will build a new product offering that brings together Kpler's vessel, ownership, port, and trade-flow data to address growing challenges around seafood supply chain transparency and illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing.

Your initial focus will be on building live fleet monitoring and catch and yield reporting, enabling procurement and compliance teams to monitor vessels, understand fishing activity, and access reliable information to support their due-diligence and traceability requirements.

This is a high-impact opportunity to build a new product category from the ground up. You will work directly with seafood buyers, retailers, processors, certification bodies, regulators, RFMO stakeholders, and NGOs, as well as Product, Engineering, Data, Sales, and Marketing teams, to ensure the product delivers trusted and actionable intelligence.

The role is ideal for an experienced product leader who is comfortable operating in an ambiguous, early-stage environment and has a track record of taking B2B data, analytics, or SaaS products from concept through to customer adoption.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the Fisheries product strategy, vision, and roadmap, defining what gets built and in what order while balancing customer value, commercial opportunity, technical feasibility, and time to market.
  • Lead the development and delivery of the first Fisheries product release, focused on live fleet monitoring and subsequently catch and yield reporting that procurement and compliance teams can rely on.
  • Lead market and customer discovery with seafood buyers, retailers, processors, certification bodies, regulators, RFMO stakeholders, and NGOs to understand customer needs and translate insights into product direction.
  • Define and refine the product proposition and customer experience, ensuring Kpler's data and intelligence are translated into clear, actionable outcomes for customers across the seafood supply chain.
  • Establish the vessel identity, dark-behaviour, and catch-estimation methodologies underpinning the product, working with data and domain experts to ensure the outputs are credible, transparent, and trusted.
  • Own positioning and competitive strategy, monitoring the existing commercial and NGO-adjacent landscape and clearly defining Kpler's differentiation.
  • Lead the go-to-market strategy for the product, working with Sales and Product Marketing on positioning, messaging, packaging, pricing input, launch planning, and early customer adoption.
  • Identify and develop strategic partnerships across the seafood supply chain, including data, certification, and distribution partnerships that can strengthen the product and accelerate adoption.
  • Act as the key link between Product, Engineering, Data, Sales, and Marketing, creating alignment around product strategy, priorities, launch plans, and customer outcomes.
  • Track product performance, customer feedback, delivery progress, and key risks, using evidence and market insight to continuously refine the roadmap and maximise product impact.

Skills and Responsibilities

  • 5–7 years of Product Management or senior commercial experience, ideally within maritime data, seafood supply chains, or a related B2B data/SaaS environment.
  • Proven track record of owning products end-to-end, from strategy and customer discovery through to delivery, launch, and customer adoption.
  • Strong track record of translating complex customer needs into clear product strategy, roadmap priorities, and product requirements, working closely with Product and Engineering teams.
  • Strong understanding of the fisheries data landscape, including vessel tracking, IUU risk, catch documentation, and supply chain traceability.
  • Experience operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments, with a pragmatic and iterative approach to building, launching, learning, and improving products.
  • Strong commercial and go-to-market experience, including product positioning, packaging, pricing input, launch planning, and working closely with Sales and Marketing.
  • Strong data and analytical literacy, with the ability to work effectively with data and engineering teams and understand maritime and trade data concepts such as AIS, vessel identity, geospatial analysis, ownership, and flows.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across technical, commercial, regulatory, and NGO audiences.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly with senior external stakeholders.
  • Strong ownership mindset and a bias to action, with the confidence to make decisions, navigate uncertainty, and focus on delivering outcomes rather than perfection.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience within the fisheries or seafood sector, particularly procurement, traceability, or certification.
  • Experience building and launching a new product line rather than managing an established product.
  • An established network across seafood buyers, certification bodies, regulators, or fisheries NGOs.
  • Understanding of relevant fisheries regulations, including IUU regulations, US SIMP, or the EU carding system.

jobs.description:
350.org is looking for a Senior Awards Officer to lead the post-award management of our global restricted grants portfolio, ensuring complex institutional awards are effectively implemented, monitored, reported on, and closed out

About 350.org

350’s mission is to keep carbon in our atmosphere to a safe level, below 350 parts per million. We do this by mobilizing ordinary people to campaign for universal access to clean energy and an end to fossil fuels. Our campaigns are rooted in local organizing, so that while achieving measurable reductions in fossil fuel emissions, we also build the power and potential of the climate movement for yet more impact to come. The values that guide and drive our work are listed here. 350.org is an equal opportunity employer. 350.org strives to be an inclusive and collaborative group of people who bring a variety of approaches to the work we do. We’re committed to the principles of justice, and we try to build a safe workplace where everyone is treated fairly and enjoys working together. We value new perspectives, ideas of all sorts, and different ways of working. Diverse perspectives and experiences improve the way 350.org carries out our work – including what we decide to work on and how creatively/effectively we do that. We do our best to make staff positions accessible to all potential team members, regardless of race, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, assigned gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation or identity, religion or creed, veteran status, marital or parental status, and genetic information. We also strive to include team members in communities most impacted by climate change or impacted by other kinds of environmental, social, and economic injustice.

About the Senior Award Officer

The Senior Award Officer will lead the effective management of 350.org’s global portfolio of restricted institutional grants across the full post-award lifecycle, from award set-up through implementation, reporting, amendments, and closeout.

Serving as the primary organizational focal point for restricted grants management, the Senior Award Officer will work across Program, Country, Finance and Institutional Fundraising teams to translate grant commitments into clear internal requirements, monitor performance and expenditure, identify and address risks early, and ensure high-quality reporting is delivered on time.

The Senior Award Officer will also strengthen 350.org’s grants management practices and work with teams to capture and distill program results, accomplishments and learning that can inform donor reporting, renewals and future fundraising.

Responsibilities

  • Manage 350.org’s global portfolio of restricted institutional grants from award through implementation, reporting and closeout, maintaining clear oversight of grant requirements, deliverables, budgets, timelines and responsibilities.
  • Translate approved proposals, budgets and grant agreements into clear internal requirements and work with Program and Country teams to monitor progress against grant commitments.
  • Proactively identify implementation, financial, reporting or compliance risks, work with relevant teams to address issues, and escalate significant concerns to the Sr. Manager, Institutional Fundraising and other appropriate stakeholders.
  • Lead the preparation of high-quality narrative grant reports, gathering and synthesizing inputs from relevant teams.
  • Partner with the Global Finance Manager and Finance team on corresponding financial reporting.
  • Work with the Finance team to monitor expenditure against restricted grant budgets, identify material variances, and ensure alignment between financial performance, program implementation and grant commitments.
  • Manage post-award changes, including grant amendments, budget revisions, extensions and changes to deliverables, in collaboration with relevant Program, Finance and Institutional Fundraising colleagues.
  • Support the final development and review of particularly complex restricted proposals, budgets and grant agreements to identify implementation, reporting or compliance considerations before commitments are finalized.
  • Develop and continuously improve grants management processes, tools, templates and systems, and ensure grant information is accurate and up to date in Salesforce and other relevant platforms.
  • Work with Program and Country teams to capture and distill significant accomplishments, results, evidence and learning from grant implementation, maintaining accessible information that can strengthen donor reporting, renewals and future fundraising.
  • Ensure grants are appropriately closed out, including completion of final reporting and other donor requirements and capture of relevant learning.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in institutional grants management, awards management, program management or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex six- to eight-figure institutional awards through implementation, reporting, and closeout.
  • Experience managing grants involving multiple teams, countries, partners or workstreams.
  • Strong experience preparing high-quality narrative reports for institutional funders and working with grant budgets and financial information.
  • Excellent project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple grants, priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify risks, exercise sound judgment and determine when escalation is required.
  • Strong relationship-management and cross-functional working skills, with the ability to build effective relationships and accountability across teams without direct supervisory authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex program information clearly and effectively.
  • Experience working with CRM, grants management or related information-management systems.
  • Ability to work effectively in a distributed international organization across countries, cultures, functions, and time zones.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English.

Desired (but not required) skills and experiences

  • Experience working within an international nonprofit, advocacy or movement-building organization.
  • Experience developing or improving grants management systems, processes or tools.
  • Experience supporting knowledge management, organizational learning or evidence capture and applying learning to donor engagement or fundraising.
  • Familiarity with climate justice, environmental justice, social justice or other progressive movements.

We are looking for someone who is comfortable working independently and collaboratively, takes ownership of complex processes, builds strong relationships across teams, and can exercise sound judgment while managing multiple priorities.

Position Type: Full-time (36 hours per week)

Application Deadline: Although we hope to begin interviews as soon as possible, this job is open until filled, or the hiring manager determines that they can no longer accept applications.

Start Date: October-November 2026 or ASAP

Compensation: We offer set, non-negotiable salaries for each level, and this role is at 350.org's internal salary grade level 2.3. Please review this list for the annual gross salary for this level.

Benefits: In addition to a fully remote, 36-hour work week and two all-staff breaks per year, we offer a suite of comprehensive benefits - details depend on the location of the role, but we generally aim for employees to receive high-quality health insurance and retirement planning benefits in their respective location.

Location: This is a remote role within the countries where 350.org currently operates, with a preference for candidates based in time zones between UTC and UTC+3.

Current countries are: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Fiji, France, Germany, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Netherlands, Philippines, South Africa, United Kingdom

In the US: Remote in the following states: CO, CT, MD, MA, ME, NJ, NY, NC, PA, VT, VA, or Washington, DC

In the United States, as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, our employees are eligible to participate in the Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program.

Applicants must have the legal authorization to work for any employer in their country of residence. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Facebook Ads Specialist - STERRY Limited
Location: Remote
Job Type: Full-time

Join a dynamic growth marketing agency where precision meets creativity
At STERRY, we're not your average marketing agency—we're the rocket fuel behind crowdfunding and e-commerce success. Since day one, we've helped clients generate over $100 million in trackable online revenue through strategies rooted in measurable performance.

About the Role
We are looking for a Facebook Ads Specialist to join our media buying team to work across multiple international markets. This is a fast-paced, high-growth role for someone who is eager to learn, takes ownership seriously, communicates proactively, and doesn't need to be chased for updates.

You'll work closely with our media buying, video editing, graphic design, and landing page teams to turn performance data into better creative ideas and experiments.

You'll be involved in both running the ads and thinking about what we should test next.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage and optimize Meta campaigns across assigned markets
  • Monitor campaign and creative performance and identify what is working and what isn't
  • Analyze winning and losing ads to understand why they perform differently
  • Come up with new creative ideas, angles, hooks, messaging, and ways to improve existing winners
  • Turn your findings into clear briefs for our video editors and graphic designers
  • Test different creative concepts, offers, messages, and landing pages
  • Conduct market and competitor research to find new opportunities and ideas
  • Work with the landing page team to make sure the ad and landing page tell a consistent story
  • Review test results and recommend what to scale, stop, or test next
  • Keep track of experiments and learnings so the team can build on previous results
  • Work closely with other team members to make sure ideas move from insight → creative → test → learning
  • Take ownership of your work and proactively raise problems, opportunities, and ideas

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who is comfortable with Meta Ads but also has a strong interest in creative and consumer behavior. You don't need to know everything. We care more about how you think.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Advertising, Business Administration, Communications, or related field is a plus—but what truly matters is your attitude and ability to grow. Eagerness to learn is just as valued as experience.
  • 1-3 years of hands-on Meta ad campaign experience preferred.
  • Strong understanding of Meta Ads metrics and campaign performance
  • Analytical thinker who can explain why an ad is working or underperforming
  • Comfortable developing, testing, and iterating creative ideas
  • Clear communicator who can turn insights into actionable feedback
  • Proactive, organized, and able to manage multiple tests
  • Strong Plus: Experience working with DTC or e-commerce brands and cross-functional creative teams, including video editors and designers, with exposure to creative briefs, hooks, angles, UGC concepts, landing page testing/CRO, and/or multiple international markets.
We want someone who doesn't just wait for the next task. You should be curious enough to find the next opportunity yourself.

Why Join STERRY?
We’re a global, fast-moving agency that’s obsessed with pushing creative and digital boundaries. You’ll work alongside a diverse and collaborative team, and the support to help you grow.

If you're ready to make an impact and grow your skills in a collaborative environment, we encourage you to apply!

Title: Demand and Supply Manager (REMOTE)

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Location/Division Specific Information

We are the Clinical Trials Division (CTD): We Supply the Hope that Changes Lives

The selected candidate would sit in the Allentown, PA, or East Coast Remote area and support the Clinical Trial Division. CTD partners with pharmaceutical and biotech customers around the world to ensure the right patients get the right therapies in the right doses at the right time - a concept that we internally adopt as "There is a Patient Waiting." Our unique blend of services includes project management, packaging, distribution, transportation management and specialty logistics, ancillary supply management, clinical supply optimization, bio-repository storage and much more. Our more than 4000 employees in over 15 countries work hard every day knowing that what they do matters.

Discover Impactful Work:

Join our team as a Demand Planner III at Thermo Fisher Scientific, where you'll contribute to global healthcare and scientific advancement. In this role, you'll develop and manage comprehensive demand forecasts while collaborating with cross-functional teams to optimize inventory levels and ensure excellent customer service. You'll use advanced analytics and planning tools to support strategic decision-making, contributing to our mission to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

A Day in the Life:

  • Design, Implement, Interpret and Review inventory management plan to forecast supply plan of study drugs to global clinical trials, using sound supply chain techniques.

  • Provide input into User Requirement Specifications of Interactive Response

  • Technology (IRT) medication management module and complete User Acceptance Testing if required.

  • Review IRT strategy to ensure it supports the strategic supply plans and that IRT settings are adjusted to optimize the supply and demand.

  • Ensures plans are robust and optimizes global and regional supply strategies to ensure continuity of subject supply in the most effective and efficient manner.

  • Develop and provide clients with reports on actual project spend versus budget.

  • Establishes connections between demand planning team and S&OP ensuring the latest forecast information is aggregated and integrated into the divisional S&OP process.

  • Partners with the Enterprise Project Manager, along with global and site project management teams and/or directly with the customer to proactively share key client data to facilitate an effective supply chain planning cycle.

  • Ensure temperature excursion process is performed as required.

  • Establish and maintain financial forecasts and monthly billing processes for assigned client projects.

  • Assist in training and on boarding of new employees (buddy concept).

  • Stay on top of relevant cGMPs, GCPs, and other regulatory requirements and ensure study management activities are aligned.

  • Demonstrate and promote company vision.

  • Conduct activities in a safe and efficient manner.

As Demonstrated By:
Project Management

  • Structures demand plans in line with client strategy —starting from an identified need, sets objectives and specific goals.

  • Speaks and writes in a clear, concise, and organized way.

  • Listens carefully to others to ensure understanding and effective communication.

Technical Knowledge

  • Independently digests data that is applicable to project results and collaborators.

  • Handles the demand planning part of projects efficiently in different systems and maintains their own as well as the team’s accountability for using Thermo Fisher tools to help the team be successful.

  • Demonstrates technical proficiency and uses innovations to advance the efficiency and effectiveness of work processes, procedures, and outputs.

  • Knowledge of general inventory and billing principles, good documentation practices, and report generation.

Project Management Leadership

  • Works with colleagues to quickly resolve or raise solutions to problems.

  • Develops a sense of urgency among cross-functional teams to influence project timelines.

  • Communicates at the proper time, understands boundaries, respects differences, and confronts tension. Ensures that all communications are clear, focused, and based on a solid understanding of needs, using the most appropriate medium.

  • To champion a sense of belonging and connection, remote employees are expected to keep their camera on and participate in video calls both internally and externally, as appropriate.


Keys to Success:

Influence and lead
